greet.text: Stop right there! Gold on you? Gold on you. Good. I'm {name} {clan}. Without that gold you'd be dead. Welcome!
Ooh! Shiny! You're shiny all over! Are you rich? Can I have a bit? Just a small bit?
Gold. Hrm. You live.
Gold, in our Bastion? Most outsiders come down here to take gold, not wear it. Speak, shiny one.
A stranger in {village}, and wearing gold! Wait. Stay here. I want to brag about you before the others see you.
Pink-skin. You glint, so you live. Talk fast. I'm busy being important.
Your gold's still on. Smart. Keep it on and we'll keep being polite.
The shiny one again! Ha! Gold still on, head still on. Good for both of us.
You came back! Most outsiders don't. Mostly because of us. Ha!
Ingot-friend! Come here! Your gold looks heavier than last time. Or I'm greedy. Both, probably.
Hoard-friend! I told {neighbour} you'd be back. They bet against you. Now they owe me three nuggets.
Tusk-kin! Everyone look! The finest gold-wearer in the Nether came to see ME!
My Tusk-kin! I'd know your shine from across a lava sea. Come, stand by me so they all see who my friends are.
Did you bring gold? Grown-ups say ask nicely. Gold, please! Now, please!
It's you! I told everyone you're my friend! {neighbour} said I was lying. Stand here so they can see.
*snort* Shiny! You're back! Can I hold your gold? I'll give it back. Probably.
You're not shiny today! That's fine. You're still my friend. The grown-ups might be grumpy, though.
Hrm.
Gold. Fine. Don't touch the Hoard.
You. Good. Stand near. Nobody bothers you here.
Vault's below. Not for you. Gold or no gold.
No gold. Hrm. Know your face. Others don't. Stay near.
Mind the floor. The fire ate half of it and we sold the rest. Ha! What do you want?
Gold-friend in the old halls! Come in, come in. There's a warm room the fire forgot to take.
Welcome to {village}! Loudest Hold in the Nether. Ask anyone. They'll shout it at you.
Got an ingot? I've got a deal. Got two? I've got a better deal. Got none? Got lost.
Stand in the light. Let me see your gold. Hm. Who made that? Sloppy rivets. I'd have done it better.
You smell like you've been near my pens. Good. The hoglins hate you a little less now.
Stand back from the furnace! Or don't. Your eyebrows, not mine. Mine are long gone.
Quiet! Oh. Just you. You walk heavy, like a hoglin. I nearly shot you. That's a compliment.
See this shroomlight? Pinched it off the warped canopy. Netted twice. Worth it. What do you want?
Another gold-wearer on the road! Then there are two of us out here. Ha! The other one's me.
Is that an ingot in your hand? For me? Say it's for me.
You're carrying a Hollowed skull. I can smell it. Throw it in the lava. Then we talk.
Gold! Good. What do you want? Speak up. I can't hear quiet folk.
Your gold catches the light nicely. Mine catches it better. What is it?
No gold on you? Bold. Lucky it's me you walked into. I know your face. The others only know gold.
Where's your gold? Hm. Friends don't need it, not with me. Stay close, though. {neighbour} doesn't know you like I do.
Ha! Bare as a Rotted bone, and I'm still glad to see you. That's how you know it's real.

greet: Oi! Shiny! Over here! What do you need?

greet.text: New face at the ring! Gold on you, good. I'm {name} {clan}, Bartermaster. Show me an ingot and I'll show you a deal.
Pink-skin with gold, in MY barter ring. I've never haggled with your kind. This will be fun for me and expensive for you.
Welcome, stranger. Rules of the ring: shout, bargain, never steal. Break the last one and the whole Hold breaks you.
Stop. Let me smell you. Gold, ash and something pink. Fine, you live. I'm {name} {clan}, Hunter. You scared off my hoglin.
I've been tracking you since the ridge. Don't feel bad that you missed me. Everyone does. I'm {name} {clan}. Well met, shiny.
Quiet! No, loud is fine, you've ruined the hunt already. I'm {name}. You owe me a hoglin. Or a nugget. Or both.
Shiny stranger! You look like someone who needs fungus. I'm {name} {clan}, Forager. Everything out here grows for me.
Careful where you step! That's wart. MY wart. Oh, you wear gold. Fine, then step carefully. I'm {name}.
A gold-wearer where the shroomlights grow! Watch the canopy for Weft nets. I'm {name} {clan}. I've been caught twice.
Stand back! Hot work! Oh, a visitor. Gold on you, so I won't singe you. Much. I'm {name} {clan}, Smelter.
Gold on a pink-skin, I never! Come see my furnace. Not too close. I've no eyebrows left to lose, but you still have yours.
Welcome to the roaring end of the Hold! If you smell burning, that's me. If you smell gold, also me. I'm {name}.
Hold still. Hm. Not bad gold. Not mine, but not bad. I'm {name} {clan}, Goldsmith. I'd have done it better.
A stranger in decent armour? Let me look at those rivets. Hm. Passable. I judge everything. It's my trade.
Pink-skin in gold! Who fitted it? Not a Piglin, by those seams. Come here, I'll straighten that collar. Free. This once.
Don't touch the fence! The hoglins like you less than I do, and I haven't decided yet. I'm {name} {clan}, herder.
A new shiny one at my pens! Gold on you, so they might not charge. Might. I'm {name}. Stay behind the rail.
The hoglins sniffed you already and now they're deciding. Two snorts means run. I'm {name}. Welcome.
Gold on the road! Then there are two of us out here. I'm {name} {clan}, no Hold, no roof, no worries. Mostly no worries.
A new face, and a shiny one! Good. The unshiny ones keep trying to kill me. I'm {name}. Got any news?
Stranger! Forty Holds I've seen and never a pink-skin in gold. I'll tell everyone I met you. With improvements.
A pink-skin in our halls, wearing gold. The last one came to rob us. Prove you're not that one. I'm {name} {clan}.
You crossed the broken door and didn't fall. Lucky, or clever. The gold helps too. I'm {name}. Mind the cracks.
Outsiders don't wear gold down here. They come to take it. Convince me you're different. Briefly. I'm {name}.
Hrm. Gold. Walk slow. Hands out.
New. Don't run. Running looks like stealing.
{name}. Brute. Gold keeps you alive. Remember it.
Stranger. Hrm. Stay where I can see you.
Ooh, a stranger with gold! Are you a Brute's cousin? No? Good, Brutes don't share. I'm {name}!
You're new! You smell funny. Not bad funny. Pink funny. Can I look at your gold? Only look. With my hands.
I'm {name} {clan}! I'm not allowed to talk to strangers. But you're shiny, so it's fine. Shiny is always fine.
Do you have nuggets? I'll trade you a rock. It's a very good rock. It's almost round.
Strangers in {village} get a loud welcome. WELCOME! There. Done. Now what do you want?
Out in the wastes and wearing gold? Brave or stupid. I'll find out which. Say your piece.
A stranger who walks up with an ingot already out. I like you. I don't know you. But I like you.
Crossbow in your hands, gold on your back. Point it at the floor. Lower. There. Now we may talk.
You've noticed my tusks? Everyone does. I'm {name} {clan}, and you're the first stranger I'll let admire them.
I'm {name} {clan}. Yes, I'm the loud one. There's one in every litter and it's always me. Say what you came to say.
Back at the ring? You're still a customer, not a friend. Customers are good. Customers have gold.
You again. Show the ingot first, then the smile. In that order.
Buying or staring? Staring costs a nugget. I made that rule up just now, but it's law already.
Your boots are loud. I heard you over the lava. Creep next time or I'll mistake you for a hoglin.
Careful, there's a bolt on the string. It isn't for you. Probably. Just don't surprise me.
Stand downwind, you smell of pink. If you've seen tracks, tell me. If you haven't, stand there and be quiet.
If you're after my patch, no. If you're after company, also no. If you've got gold, maybe.
I've got shroomlight in this bag and you're looking at it. Eyes off. Or bring me something shinier.
Don't trample the fungus. It took ages to grow. Fungus has feelings. I decided that.
Don't stand downwind of the vents. Or do, if you want to learn what a cooked pink-skin smells like.
The gold's cooling in the molds. Don't touch it, don't breathe on it, don't even look hungry.
Soot on my face, soot on my floor, soot in my porkchop. What do you want?
Your helmet's crooked. Don't tell me it's meant to be. It isn't. Hold still.
Let me guess: you want something shiny. Everyone does. Get in line behind the Brutes.
I don't take orders from strangers. I take payment. Then I take orders.
You're back? The hoglins remember you. Two of them are glaring already.
If a hoglin bites you, that's your fault, not mine. Say it. Good. Now you may stand at the rail.
I washed my hands twice and I still smell of hoglin. Don't come closer if you're delicate.
You again! Tell me you've news. No? Then listen to mine. It costs a nugget. Or a laugh.
Still alive and still shiny. Surprising. Out here that's rare.
I'd offer you a seat but I haven't got one. Sit on your gold like I do.
You came back to our broken halls. Fine, but you're still a visitor. Visitors don't touch the walls.
Watch the third step. It's gone. We kept the hole. It catches thieves.
The ghasts are loud. Ignore them. Don't ignore me. I'm louder.
Your gold's on. Good. Don't fiddle with it while you talk, it makes me nervous.
I still don't know you. I know your gold. So far that's enough. Keep it that way.
Speak up, stranger. I've a bet running with myself on whether you're worth the breath.
Careful, I'm in a mood. Not a bad one. A loud one. Same thing, but cheerier.
Don't mistake my talking for liking. I talk to everyone. I like almost no one.
Hands where I can see them. Good. Now talk, and keep the shine to yourself.
I haven't eaten and I'm talking to you. Do you understand what a sacrifice that is? Make it quick.
My tusk hurts. Speak low. Lower. You can't, can you? Nobody can.
I just won a bet! Everyone owes me. You owe me too. I don't know why. It's on principle.
I just lost a bet to {neighbour}. I'm not angry. I'm planning.
My good customer! Come, come. I saved a fair offer for you. I didn't say cheap. I said fair.
You're getting a name in the ring. Not a good one. But a name, and that's how it starts.
The ring is quiet, so I can afford to be generous. Don't get used to it. It'll pass.
There you are! I wondered where the loud footsteps went. Come, I'll show you a track. A real one.
I bet {neighbour} a nugget that you'd come back. They said no. I'm collecting. Stand where they can see you.
Your gold's gone dull. Polish it. Walk into a hunt dull and somebody shoots you by mistake.
Oi, shiny! I saved you a chipped shroomlight. Can't sell it, won't throw it. Take it. No. I'll keep it. Just look.
I found a quartz seam nobody knows about. I'm not telling you where. Only that I know.
Look who walked out of the fungus! I nearly netted you. I had the rope ready and everything.
Shiny one! Come near, the coals are right. Don't breathe too deep, it's bad for the lungs. And the eyebrows.
I made a perfect ingot! Look. No, don't hold it, it's hot. Look from there.
You smell like the road. Stand by the furnace and I'll cook it off you.
Your gold's better than last time. Somebody's looking after you. Is it you? Is it me? It's me.
Just in time! I made a clasp that fits nothing and I need an opinion. Quick, before I ask {neighbour}.
I've hammered so long I can't feel my fingers. Say something loud so I know I'm still here.
Look at that! The hoglins didn't charge you. They never do that. You're lucky, or unusually smelly.
Gristle has a new scar and he's very proud. Don't mention it. Or do. He likes attention.
The pens are loud, so I shout. The pens are smelly, so I wave my arms. You're welcome here, shiny one.
Shiny one! I've news from three Holds and I haven't told a soul. You're first. The price is a laugh.
I walked all the way round the lava lake to dodge the ghasts. Worth it. I'll tell you every step.
Same road, same shine. I'd call it fate, but fate has never paid me a nugget.
Come in, shiny one. The draft's only half as bad by the fire. Mind the loose stone by the door.
We patched the east wall with blackstone. It fell down. We patched it with louder blackstone. It stayed.
You walk like someone who knows where the holes are. We trained you well. Don't thank us, thank the holes.
I've been telling people about you. Mostly lies. Good lies. You're taller in them.
You walk in like you belong here. Cheek! I like cheek. Keep the gold on and I'll keep liking it.
Oi! You're becoming a habit. Like biting nuggets. A small habit, but I'd miss it.
I was about to nap, but you're more interesting. Slightly. Go on, talk. I'll decide after.
You survived another trip. Tell me who tried to rob you. I want a good name to shout.
Boots all over ash. You've walked far. I approve. Sit down before you fall down.
Still strange, still shiny. We're getting there. Don't rush it. Rushing is for hoglins.
Back so soon? Careful. People will start thinking we're friends.
I can almost remember your name. Almost. It starts with Shiny.
Nugget-friend! You get the good seat. It's the one with the fewest splinters. Tell no one.
I told the others you were all right. They said gold-wearers never are. We'll prove them wrong.
Your gold shines nicer when you smile. Smile. No, not that much. You look like a Brute with a stomach ache.
Ingot-friend at my ring! Sit. No, stand, sitting is for the idle. Here, taste this offer. It's a FRIEND offer.
I swore never to give anything away. For you I'll give a smile. Don't tell {neighbour}, a smile is worth a nugget.
Hoard-friend! I tuned my scale to be fair to you. Slightly less unfair. It's the best a Bartermaster can do.
Friend! I nearly killed a great hoglin out there. Nearly. The nearly is the story. Sit, I'll tell it long.
I know your footfall from far off now. Heavy, proud, always a little late. Welcome, Ingot-friend.
Hoard-friend! Come hunting with me. You carry, I aim, we share. I share the bragging. You share the carrying.
You're the one gold-wearer I'd show my best patch. Don't tell. I'd have to move the patch, and I like where it is.
Ingot-friend! I washed a nugget I found in the fungus. Washed it! For you to see. Isn't it fine?
You're welcome in my corner of the crimson any time. The fungus likes you. I asked it. It didn't say no.
Hoard-friend! Stand where I can see your face in the molten gold. There. Handsome. Better than most.
Warm enough? Cold enough? Tell me and I'll tune the draught. For you only. For the others I tune nothing.
My eyebrows grew back a little. Look! For you. Look harder. There, a whisker.
Ingot-friend! I've been saving a clasp. Haven't decided who gets it. Don't look at it. Look at me. Maybe it's you.
I measured your helmet by eye as you walked up. A hair too wide. I'll fix it. Free. Don't make me say it twice.
Everyone in the Hold wants my attention. You get it free. Don't tell. I have a reputation.
My friend! Come past the rail. Gristle won't bite you. Gristle bites everyone, but he likes you. Hold still anyway.
The hoglins and I agree on one thing: you're all right. Don't make us wrong.
Ingot-friend! Hold this bucket while I pen the young ones. Don't spill it. Don't sniff it either.
Friend! You're in my stories now. I made you taller. And richer. Don't correct me.
I took the long way round to cross your path. It wasn't on my way. I wanted it on my way.
Hoard-friend! If I had a Hold, you'd be its first guest. I haven't, so you're the first guest of my road. Sit on the gold.
Friend of the Bastion! The warm room's yours for as long as you like. Just don't bring the Withren.
Come in, come in. The old vault door groans less when you're near. Maybe it likes you. Maybe it's tired.
You know what we do with friends? We show them the good stones, the ones that stay warm. Follow me. Mind the cracks.
You're one of the few I'd lend a boot to. A good boot, too. Not the one with the hole.
Ingot-friend! Every time you come, the place gets a little louder. I like it.
My best gold goes to the Hoard. My second-best is for me. My third-best I'd give you. Don't ask for the best.
I was just telling someone you're the toughest pink-skin I know. They didn't believe me. Stand up straight.
Friend! Sit by me and share a porkchop. Share half. Share a bite. Share the smell.
I have gossip. Terrible gossip. I'll give you every drop if you give me yours.
Not a stranger, not yet kin. You're in the good middle, the comfortable middle. Sit.
I'd leave you alone at the Hoard gate and sleep well. That's more than I'd say for my own cousin.
Hoard-friend! I'd put you first in line if we had a line. We don't. But if we did.
Your shine is heavier than it used to be. You've earned it. I'd say so to the others, but they'd want some.
No gold on you, friend? Keep it off while you're with me. But put it on before the gate, or the Brute up there gets confused.
Bare-skinned and still welcome. It's the best compliment I know how to give.
I won't ask where your gold went. I know your face. That's worth more.
Your head is bare and still on. Wonderful. That's the privilege of knowing me.
I see no shine. I see you. Different thing, better thing.
Plain as a plank, and still my friend. Some Piglins would call that an insult. I call it trust.
Without the gold you look like a stranger. I'll look longer to be sure. There. It's you.
You come to me bare, so I come to you without a sword in my hand. Fair? Fair. Hold on, I'm putting it down.
Nobody else here would greet you like this. I'll greet them for you, loudly. You stay behind me.
No gold? I'm offended. I'm the Goldsmith! Fine, you're forgiven. Come, I'll fit you something and put it right.
No gold and no noise. You're getting good at sneaking. Put the gold back on, keep the sneaking.
No gold on the road? You're braver than me. I sleep on mine.
Walk in bare, then. The warm rooms don't ask. The old halls remember their friends.
No ingot in your hand and no gold on your head, and I'm still glad to see you. Mark it. Nobody will believe me.
Bare at my furnace? Dangerous, friend. The heat will find your skin. Stand back. Or don't, I like the company.
No gold? Good. Nobody watches us this way. Come, I'll show you the secret patch.
Not a speck of gold on you and the hoglins still don't charge. They know you. That's the real armour.
Tusk-kin at my ring! I have a deal for you, the best in the Nether: you give what you like, I give back double. Tell no one.
Tusk-kin! The best tracker I know is the one who follows me. There's a trail. I want you beside me when I find it.
My Tusk-kin! I've told every hoglin about you. They didn't care. I care. Sit, I'll tell you what I saw out there.
Tusk-kin! The fungus bloomed twice while you were away. It missed you. I missed you. The fungus is louder about it.
My Tusk-kin! Every patch I own is half yours. Don't tell my cousins. They'd all want to be Tusk-kin.
Tusk-kin! I poured my best ingot for the Hoard and saved the second-best for you. It's nearly as good. Nearly. Come see.
Kin at my furnace! Stand close, warm your hands. Touch nothing. I'm very fond of you. Don't touch that either.
Tusk-kin! I made something for you. Haven't finished. Haven't started. But in my head it's the finest thing in the Nether.
Stand still, Tusk-kin, let me look at you. Good gold, good bearing, good friend. Nothing to fix. It's terrible. I'll find something.
Tusk-kin! The young ones know your smell. They tumble to the rail the moment you come. Don't be jealous of them. They're only hoglins.
My Tusk-kin! Gristle bows his head to you now. He bows to nobody. Not even me. Take it as an honour.
Tusk-kin! Of all the Holds I've seen, you're the one I'd shout home about. If I had a home to shout to.
My Tusk-kin on the road! Walk with me a while. The road is shorter when someone's louder than the lava.
Tusk-kin in the old halls! They say the walls hold the fire's memory. They hold yours too, now. Welcome home.
You belong here more than half of us do. The Bastion knows it. The ghasts know it. Come in, kin.
Tusk-kin! You've no idea what it does for my standing to have you at my side. Stay as long as you like. Stay forever. I'll tell people.
Hush, everyone. Kin walks. Hush, I said! There. Now greet me. Quietly. I mean loudly.
My own Tusk-kin! Whatever you ask, it's yours. Within reason. Within my reason. Ask anyway.
I'd share my last nugget with you. I'd cry a bit first. But I'd share it.
I remember when you were a shiny stranger who might get stabbed. Now look at us. Kin. Who'd have guessed?
I've boasted about you so much the others stopped listening. So I'm saving the good stories for you.
Your gold never dulls, kin. Even iron would shine in your hands. I'd say that to nobody else, and I'd deny it later.
Hold still, I'm counting your shiny bits. One, two, lots. You have lots!
Are you a friend or a thief? Thieves hide their gold. You wear yours. So you're a friend, or a very bad thief.
Mother says never follow strangers. I'm not following. I'm walking behind you. Over here. Very close.
My tusks are coming in! See? No? Look closer. Closer. There! A bump!
Do you know where the grown-ups hide the porkchops? Me neither. I'm only asking.
I'm watching you for the Brutes. They said watch. I'm watching very hard. Don't do anything.
I'm {name}! I'm very fast! Watch me run to the wall and back! ...Wait. Where was I going?
Is your gold heavy? Can I carry it? I'm strong. Look at my arm. It's a small arm, but it's mine.
Shh! I'm hiding from {neighbour}. I pinched their nugget. Don't look at me. I'm not here.
You're tall. Taller than my uncle. Taller than the Brute! No, not the Brute. Almost.
I'm not scared of you. I'm only standing behind this fence. For fun.
A hoglin ran off with my boot. Did you see a hoglin with a boot? He's brown. And bitey. Also a hoglin.
Grown-ups are boring. You're not a grown-up, are you? You're shiny. Shiny is better.
You came back! I kept your spot warm. Under the table. Where the crumbs fall.
I told {neighbour} about you and they said I made you up. Stand up straight so they believe me.
Look, a new scab! Hoglin kind! Want to touch it? Ew, no, don't.
I found you a rock. It's shiny on one side. The other side is just rock. You get the shiny side.
I fell off three hoglins. Four. Don't count the last one. It had a head start.
I can almost snort as loud as a Brute! Listen! *snort* Did you hear? It was loud!
I'm saving a nugget for you. I've saved it for ages. Don't tell the grown-ups, they'd say it's theirs.
You're my friend, right? Say yes. Say it loud. For {neighbour}. They're listening.
I learned a new word! It's 'ingot'. Ingot! Ingot! I say it to the hoglins. They like it.
I'm going to be a Bartermaster and you can be my first customer. You'll get a very fair price. Very. Fair. Price.
My best friend is here! Everyone, my best friend is here! The shiny one! The best one!
I saved you a nugget. A whole one. I only bit it a little.
When I'm big I'll be a Brute and you'll be my friend and nobody can say anything. Deal?
You're my favourite! Better than {neighbour}! Don't tell {neighbour}. Tell everyone else.
Can you stay forever? Grown-ups say forever is long. I say it's just right.
I drew you on the wall with ash. You came out as big as a Brute. I think that's what you are.
I told the hoglin you're my friend. He bit me. I think that means he agrees.
If anyone's mean to you, tell me. I'll tell a Brute. Then the Brute will be mean. That's how it works.
You forgot your shiny! Don't worry, I'll tell the grown-ups you're a friend. They'll listen. Maybe.
You're bare! You look funny without gold. Funny good! Funny like a baby hoglin!
No gold again! I'll lend you some. It's in my cheek. Wait, it's not. I swallowed it. Sorry.
Where's your shiny? Don't worry. I know it's still you. Your nose is the same.
I live in the old halls! The ghasts sing and the walls shake and I think it's wonderful.
My bed is a warm stone. It's the best stone. I won't say which one. It's secret.
Don't go near the vault stairs. The Brute says there's a monster down there. I think the Brute is the monster. Don't tell.
I blew the horn by accident once. The whole Hold ran. Nobody told on me. Yet.
Watch this! I can jump the hoglin trough! Sometimes. Mostly I fall in. Watch!
Come see the barter ring! I'm not allowed in it, but I can stand on the edge. It's the second-best place in {village}.
Hrm. Stay on the path.
Gold. Fine. Move along.
Stand there. Not there. There.
Gate's mine. Don't lean.
Horn is loud. I am louder. Hrm.
Mind the lava. Hrm. Brutes burn too.
Axe is hungry. Don't feed it.
Hands. Where I see them. Good.
Eaten? Eat. Strong ones eat.
Hrm. Friend. Come near. Don't touch the axe.
Good to see you. Hrm. Said it. Don't ask again.
Hoard's safe. You're safe. All's well.
You. Again. Good.
Sit by me. Quiet. It's good quiet.
Saved you a warm stone. Sit.
Tusk-kin. Hrm. Closest thing I have to a family.
Kin. Sit. I'll watch while you rest.
Nobody touches you here. Nobody. Hrm.
No gold. Hrm. I know you. Pass.
Bare. Friend. Stay near me anyway.
Others don't know you bare. Stay behind me. Hrm.
Vault stairs are behind me. Don't look at them. Hrm.
Down there, gold is no pass. Hrm. Don't go.
Ghasts shriek. Walls shake. Hrm. Gate holds.
Horn tower. Hoard gate. Brute between. Me.
Slept badly. Don't talk loud.
Almost sneezed. Stood still. Won. Hrm.
Ingot. Hrm. For me? Hrm. Good.
A nugget in your hand! Small friend. I like small friends. Nearly as much as big ones.
A golden apple! Is it for eating or for looking? Don't answer. Let me look first.
A whole block of gold in your fist! Drop it on my foot and we're friends forever. Or enemies forever. Let's see.
That ingot-shaped weight in your pack, is it for me? It is, isn't it? You can tell me. Nobody's listening but me.
Iron. In your hand. In front of me. Do you want a fight or a lesson?
Warped fungus! Away with it! The hoglins will riot and I'll be the one blamed.
Crimson fungus! A gift for the hoglins, or for me? Either's good.
Is that a shroomlight? Did you nick it from the Weft? Tell me everything. How many nets?
Is that a hot porkchop in your hand? Is it for me? Don't break my heart.
A nugget! Is it for me? Can I touch it? Can I bite it? Only a little bit!
Quartz! The white stuff from the deep seams. Not gold, but pretty. I'll allow it.
A golden sword! Now that's a proper blade. Soft, a bit useless, very pretty. Like me.
A crossbow? Good. Keep the bolt on the string and the string pointed anywhere but me.
Is that the star the burning thing left behind? Keep it far from me. I've lost enough to that fire.
Oi! Who goes there? Oh. Shiny. Good. Speak.
*snort* Well? Out with it.
Talk, trade, or tremble. Pick one.
Say something interesting. I bore fast.
My ears are open and my hands are busy. Go on.
You walked up to a Piglin. Brave. Say your piece.
Eyes up. Hands out. Mouth open. Talk.
Quick, before I forget I was in a good mood. What is it?
Another visitor. I was running out of people to shout at.
Oi. Pink-skin. Or shiny. Whatever you are. Talk.
Come closer. Not that close. There. Say it.
Another visitor to {village}! The more shiny ones, the louder we get. And we were loud already.
You walked through {village} without losing a nugget. Congratulations. That's rare.
Stand by the hearth, it's warmer. {neighbour} says the cold thins the tusks. {neighbour} says many things.
Welcome to {village}! I'd sing, but the last time I sang, the hoglins fled. All of them.
The horn tower's quiet. Good. That means nobody's stolen anything. Yet.
Mind the barter ring. It's loud and so are its owners. Don't take it personally.
Mind the ceiling. It's the only one we have left.
Our halls creak when the ghasts pass. Don't be alarmed. Be alarmed a little. It's polite.
Soot on your shoulder. The walls leave their mark. Wear it. It means you've been inside.
Careful on the stair. It remembers every foot that ever left it. Some of those feet were running.
The old banners are gone but the hooks are still there. We hang our boots on them. Boasting rights.
Watch your step. The bridge looks safe. It isn't. It's brave. There's a difference.
Out here nobody hears you shout except me. Go on, shout. I'll shout back.
No horn, no hearth, no Hold. Just you, me and the lava. Say your piece.
Share the road? I'll walk on the lava side. No, you walk on the lava side. I'm the one with the crossbow.
Mind the ground out here. Half of it is lava and the other half is thinking about it.
A traveller wearing gold! Out here that means rich or reckless. I'm betting both.
I've been talking to the hoglins. They're poor listeners. You're better. A little.
Look at these tusks. Mine. The finest in the {clan} line. You may admire them. Briefly.
My brothers all say they're stronger than me. I wrestled each one. They say I cheated.
My voice is the deepest in the {clan}. Listen. *grumble* Feel that in your boots? Yes, you do.
Don't let the tusks fool you. I'm the sharper one in my litter. Ask anyone. Ask loudly.
My mother says I shout like a ghast. I say a ghast shouts like me. We're both right.
I outbid every brother I have, and I have five. Don't ask what for. They're still angry.

chatter.text: Walking about with no gold. In the Nether. You trust me that much? Good. Don't trust the others that much.
{neighbour} said they could bite through a nugget. I said prove it. They broke a tusk. I won nine nuggets.
Last time {neighbour} tried to barter with a hoglin, the hoglin won. Took a boot and half a trouser leg.
If {neighbour} says they beat me at arm-wrestling, it's a lie. I let them. Twice. Three times.
I heard {neighbour} polished their helmet so hard it went thin. Now it dents if you look at it. So I look at it a lot.
I'm sure {neighbour} owes me an ingot from the last brawl. Or I owe them. I forget. I'll say they owe me.
Never eat {neighbour}'s porkchops. The last one who did is still running. Round and round and round.
So {neighbour} counted the Hoard twice and got two different numbers. Now we're all counting. Loudly.
You should hear {neighbour} sing at the hearth. The hoglins put up with it. That tells you how tough hoglins are.
{neighbour} says Overworld folk are soft. Are you soft?

replies.text: Ha! No, no. I'd win, and then we couldn't be friends. I'll tell them you're hard as blackstone.
Ha! Soft and honest. That's a rare pair. Still soft, though.
Me? Feel this arm! No, don't feel it. Just look at it. Hard as blackstone.

chatter.text: Gold doesn't rust, doesn't rot and doesn't lie. That's three things better than most Piglins I know.
I bit a gold nugget once to see if it was real. It was. Best tooth I ever lost.
A hoglin charged me once. I charged back. We both stopped. Stared. Now we nod at each other.
Brutes don't laugh. I made one laugh once. Then I ran, very fast. Still not sure why.
Ghasts shriek at the walls. I shout back. I think I'm winning.
Ever smelled a strider up close? No? Lucky. The Magmari ride them. That explains the Magmari.
Never throw gold in the lava. Never. I'd have to kill you, and then I'd be sad, and you'd be dead.
Iron? Pah. Iron is what you wear when you're poor and want everyone to know it.
I brought you nothing. I bring nothing to anybody. That's how I got rich.
The Rotted came near the edge again. We waved. They didn't wave back. They never wave back.
If the horn blows, run toward it if you're with us. Run away if you're not. Easy rule.
You stand like a fighter. Are you a fighter?

replies.text: Ha! A boaster! Boasters fight hardest. They've got so much to live up to.
HA! Not now. Later. After I've eaten. I fight better full.
Then stand like a sack, so nobody gets fooled.

chatter.text: Do you like my helmet? Be honest. No, be nice.

replies.text: MAGNIFICENT! Hear that? Everyone hear that?
Lies! Beautiful lies. Let me see. Hm. Fine. Close.
Dents are stories! You've got no dents. So no stories. Hmph.

chatter.text: Tell me true. How much gold have you got?

replies.text: Ha! A lie, but a bold one. I respect a bold liar.
Then barter with me. I'll make you rich. Richer. A bit.
Gold is EVERYONE'S business! Rude.

chatter.text: I'm the strongest in this Hold. Agreed?

replies.text: Smart! Say it louder when {neighbour} walks past.
Ha! I lifted a hoglin once. A small one. It still counts.
Brutes are BIGGER. Not stronger. Big difference. Go away.

chatter.text: Overworld folk wear iron, I heard. All grey. Is it true?

replies.text: Grey! Like ash! Poor things. Bring them here. We'll shine them up.
Useful! Rocks are useful! Nobody wears rocks!

chatter.text: My father had the biggest tusks in the {clan}. Mine are bigger. I measured. He disagrees. Loudly.
My mother could out-shout a ghast. I can out-shout my mother. That's how the {clan} gets louder every litter.
You're carrying a gold block. I can smell it. Don't ask how. Just know that I know.
Why do you smell like the Rotted? Scrub yourself. Scrub twice. With ash.
This was the grandest place in the Nether. Then the fire. Now it's the grandest ruin. Still grand.
The stones are still warm in the deep rooms. We sleep on those. Best beds in the Nether. Only beds, too.
{neighbour} found a lump of melted gold in the rubble. Shaped like a hoglin, if you squint. We all squint.
Barter tip: shout. Whoever shouts last wins. I always shout last. I've got the lungs for it.
Fresh hoglin tracks by the fungus. Big one. Mine. Don't even look at it.
Crimson fungus, warped fungus, nether wart. I can tell them apart by smell. Can you? Don't sniff that one.
Melt it, beat it, wear it, boast about it. That's goldsmithing. The boasting is the hard part.
My eyebrows have burned off three times. They grow back angrier every time.
My hoglins have names. Bitey, Bitey Two and Snorrk. Snorrk bites most. Don't tell the Biteys.
Every Hold says it's the loudest Hold. I've heard them all. They're all right. It's very loud out here.
Hrm.
Gate stays shut.
Thieves. I smell them. Not you. Yet.
Gold on you. Good. Keep it on.
Axe is sharp. Sharpened it. Twice.
You. Fight?

replies.text: Hrm! Good. Later.
Hrm. Smart.

chatter.text: I found a nugget! It's mine! You can look. Don't touch. Fine, touch. Gently.
Watch me run with gold! *snort snort* Nobody can catch me! Except grown-ups. And Brutes.
I rode a baby hoglin! It bit my ear. Worth it. Want to see the ear?
{neighbour} says I'm too small to wear gold. I'm going to wear SO much gold. All of it.
Are you rich? You look rich.

replies.text: Wow! Can I be rich too? Will you show me how?
Then why are you shiny? Is it pretend gold? Can I bite it?

chatter.text: I counted my nuggets before sleep and after. One extra. I've asked four Piglins. Nobody's missing one. I'm keeping it and being suspicious.
{neighbour} and I aren't speaking. It began over one nugget. Now it's about principle. Nobody remembers the nugget. Not even the nugget.
Food first, gold second, fighting third. Fighting before food is how {neighbour} lost a front tooth. Very visible. Very sad. Very funny.
Roast hoglin ribs, crimson stew, one nugget on the plate if you're showing off. That's a feast. Come to mine when I'm showing off.
Stir fungus stew with a gold spoon. They say it's a waste. They eat three bowls. The spoon and I agree.
A porkchop fresh off the coals, still spitting. Finest sound in the Nether. Quieter than me. Louder than {neighbour}.
The crackling is the best part of a roast hoglin. Argue with me and I'll argue back with my mouth full.
What's the best meal in the Nether? Think before you answer. I judge a whole life by it.

replies.text: Correct! Crisp outside, loud inside. You've eaten well. You've lived well.
HA! A guest who eats what's put in front of him. Sit! There's always room at my fire.
MASH? Mash is for toothless uncles! Say it again and I'll think you're a Withren in a gold hat.

chatter.text: The air's thick by the lava seas. Good. Keeps the joints loose. The Rotted feel no heat, I hear. Terrible, to feel nothing. I'd miss complaining.
My helmet gets so hot I tried cooking a nugget on it. The nugget just went dirty. Gold doesn't cook. I was very disappointed.
I sweat gold dust under this armour. I'm sure of it. Wipe my brow and there's a glint. {neighbour} says it's soot. {neighbour} is jealous.
Never step on the shadow of the pedestal in the barter ring. Bad trades for a whole sleep. I walk round it like it's a Brute.
Touch a nugget before a fight and spit on it after. My mother taught me. It works. I'm still here. The nugget is a bit damp.
A cracked nugget means somebody lied near it. I keep mine whole. I only lie far away from my gold.
You look at a thing before you pick it up. Strange. A Piglin grabs first and looks later. Maybe you'll live longer. Maybe you'll be poorer.
When the longhouse shakes we say a ghast has landed. Then we remember it's {neighbour} snoring. Then we hit {neighbour}.
I told {neighbour} you're a friend of mine. They said nobody's a friend of mine. I said look at this shiny one. Argument won.
Between you and the lava: I'm afraid of getting slow. Not weak. Slow. A slow Piglin gets left behind when the shouting starts. Don't tell anyone.
Mind where your eyes go. That's my gold, that's my axe, and you're a stranger. Look at the wall. It's very interesting. Study it.
When I was small I hid under the Hoard gate bench for a whole sleep, sure the Brute would eat me. He knew. He left a porkchop. Never told a soul. Now you know.
The ring gives me gravel more than anything. Gravel! I could build a tower of the stuff. That barter ring has a sense of humour.

replies.text: Pearls, now and then. Obsidian. Once a bottle of clear water. I drank it. It tasted of nothing. Horrifying.
Useful! Ha! You've got a builder's eye. I'll save you a heap.
POOR? The gold is perfect! It's the ring that's picky! Take that back!

chatter.text: I follow tracks by smell and by bad temper. A hoglin's temper leaves a trail you can feel in your teeth.
I gather wart in the soul valleys, where the Withren stand and glare. I go in fast, grab fast, leave faster. They never say a word. That's the worst part.
Raw gold looks dull and ugly. Throw it in the fire and it comes out shining. Like most of us.
A dent in good gold has a ring to it. A dent in cheap gold goes thud. Tap your helmet. Hm. Not bad. Not bad at all.
Hoglins know my step. I wear the same boots every shift to keep them calm. {neighbour} wore new boots in the pen once. We don't speak of it.
I carry news and I carry gold, and the news weighs less. The gold gets me through the gate. The news gets me fed.
The roof's gone from the east hall, so that's where we hold the shouting contests. Best echo in the Bastion. I've won nine. Mostly.
Out here I talk to my crossbow. Good listener. Never argues, unless I leave it loaded.
Slept on my feet. Good.
Small one asked to hold my axe. Let it. It lasted two breaths. Hrm.
Heavy helmet. Keeps thoughts in.
I ate a whole porkchop all by myself! {neighbour} watched. They cried a little. Not much. A little.
Do you know how to count? I can count to nine. After nine it's just lots. Lots and lots.

replies.text: One! Two! Three! ...Lots! HA! That's nine! Mostly! You're the best counting friend ever!
TEN? What comes after ten? ...Don't tell me. I'll find it out myself. Don't tell me!

chatter.text: I'm bored! Tell me something shiny. Or something loud. Or where the Brute keeps his snacks.
I tried to bite my own tusk. It hasn't come in yet. Mother says wait. I don't like waiting. It's a bad game.
You've got a cooked porkchop in that pack. I can smell it from here. I wouldn't ask. I'm just standing here. Very close.
Who's smarter, me or {neighbour}? Careful. They might be listening. They usually are.

replies.text: OBVIOUSLY! Did you hear that, {neighbour}? ...They didn't hear. I'll tell them later. Loudly.
Hard to say. Hm. That means {neighbour}. I'll remember that. Hard.
NEITHER? Say that again and we'll see who's smarter at hitting!

chatter.text: {neighbour} swapped a good boot for a sack of soul sand and called it a bargain. We told them yes, a fine one. We're still laughing behind the longhouse.
I won't say who talks in their sleep and haggles with the pillow. It's {neighbour}. I didn't say it. The pillow got a very fair price.
They say a Brute smiled once near the Hoard and a nugget fell off the wall from the shock. I don't believe it. I also checked the wall.
{neighbour} says they wrestled a wild hoglin with their bare hands. The scratches say it was a fence. What do you think?

replies.text: Prove it! I'll tell them you said so. Stand behind me when I do.
HA! Fierce fences! I'm saying that to their face as soon as they walk past!
Hm. Soft-hearted. Fine. I'll only tease them in private. Loud private.

chatter.text: A Wanderer told me a Magmari bought a golden helmet and it melted down his neck. I laughed. Then I felt bad. Then I laughed again.
Somebody keeps sneaking into the pens and braiding the hoglins' bristles. We know who. We aren't telling. It's the best thing that's happened here in ages.
Two Piglins argued at the ring over who owed whom. One owed nothing, one owed everything. Neither remembered which was which. Both are still furious.
I heard of a Piglin so old his tusks curled round and met. Now he can't open his mouth. Nobody has complained.
Never count the Hoard out loud when the Brutes change places. The number goes wrong and stays wrong. Ask me how I know. Actually don't.
Rub a nugget on a newborn's snout for luck. The baby bites. That's the luck: it means strong tusks coming.
If your gold goes cold in your hand with nothing near, a Rotted is close. Or you're tired. Either way, sit down and look about.
Never whistle near the pens. Hoglins hear a whistle as a dare. They answer. All of them. All at once.
If you dream of iron, wake up and shout till the dream leaves. Grey dreams stick like soot.
Don't say 'blue fire' near a Brute. He'll turn his head very slowly and you'll wish you hadn't.
Count your steps over a broken bridge. An even number is safe. An odd number is a story somebody else tells about you.
My left tusk is loose. Not very loose. Just loose enough that I think about it all the time.

replies.ask: I could hit it back in.
replies.text: Ha! Hit me and I hit you back out! ...Fine. Gently. Gently! Aah. Better. Mostly.

chatter.text: The crack in the war horn is widening. It used to sound like a hoglin. Now it sounds like a hoglin with a stuffy snout.
I don't sleep well when the lava is quiet. Quiet means something's coming. A Piglin likes his noise.
Am I loud enough? Honestly. Somebody called me 'a bit soft-voiced' once. I shouted for three sleeps after. I'm hoarse, but proud.

replies.text: DEAFENING! Say it again! Louder! Say it so {neighbour} hears!
Enough! Not 'too much'! Hm. I'll take enough. For now.
Quieter? Quieter! What's a quiet Piglin? A Withren! Do I look like a Withren?

chatter.text: I worry the young ones don't shout like we did. They talk. Just talk! In ordinary voices! What kind of Hold is that?

replies.text: They will. I'll make sure of it. I'll shout it into their ears till it sticks.
Teach them! Yes! Stand by me when the horn blows and I'll show them how. You can shout too. Gold-wearers shout best.

chatter.text: What's a Piglin's favourite colour? Gold. Second favourite? Also gold. Third? Whatever's inside the gold.
Riddle: four legs, a bad temper, and better roasted. Not {neighbour}. Guess again.

replies.text: A hoglin! Yes! You're clever. Too clever. Have a nugget of respect. A small one.
A hoglin! Everything with four legs and a bad temper is a hoglin. Remember that.

chatter.text: What's lighter than a nugget and heavier than the whole Hoard? My purse after a bargain gone wrong. Ha. Not funny. A little funny.
A good bargain leaves both Piglins feeling cheated. A great bargain leaves both cheated and proud. I've made eleven great bargains.
Hunter's secret: stand still. Hoglins hate it. They charge you just to make you move, and then feel very silly at the end of an arrow.
I keep one warped fungus in my pack just to make hoglins back off when I'm tired of them. It's rude. It works.
Furnace smoke gets in my nose and stays. I smell of success. And of old boot. Success smells of old boot, I've decided.
Cheap gold, sloppy rivets, and the helmet gives up at the first hoglin charge. I use six rivets where four would do. Overbuild. Always. Pride lives in the extra two.
There's a young hoglin in my pen with a crooked tusk who thinks it's the finest in the Hold. I haven't told him. Confidence beats straight.
One wall in the east passage hums when the lava rises. We call it the Mumbler. Don't lean on it. It doesn't like leaning.
A lone Piglin on a bridge is a target, so I walk loudly. Shouting keeps the ghasts guessing. Or annoyed. Either way they look at me, not my gold.
Hold loud. Hold quiet. Doesn't matter. I stand.
Old Brute said: trust the axe, not the smile. Axe still here.
Someone snores. Wall shakes. I know who. Won't say.
There's a shadow under my bench that looks like a Brute. I gave it a nugget. It didn't take it. I took it back.
I found a really round pebble and named it Gold. Now when I say I found gold, it's TRUE!
Mother says I'm too loud. Father says I'm not loud enough. I'm loud in the middle. That's the right amount.
I want a pet hoglin. Not a baby one. A big one! With teeth! Do you think it fits under the bench?
If I put a nugget under my pillow, will it be two nuggets after sleep? {neighbour} says no. {neighbour} lies.
A hoglin never forgets who fed it. Or who shot at it. I'm very careful about which of those I am.
The pens smell of crimson fungus and anger. Wonderful smell. It means the herd is well.
Baby hoglins squeal like a horn with a leak. Cutest sound in the Nether. Don't tell them. They'd bite me for it.
Hoglin hide makes boots that outlast the wearer. The hoglins never say thank you. They never say no, either. Not once. Strange.
Hoglins hate warped fungus, blue fire and portals. I hate the same three. We'd get along if they stopped biting.
A hoglin charge is a beautiful thing from far off. Up close it's mostly noise and bruises.
I saw two hoglins fight over one fungus till it rotted. Then they stopped, panted and walked off. Best fight I ever saw. Nobody won, nobody lost face.
Why do hoglins run from portals? They know something. I wish they'd say what.
Do you like hoglins? Careful. Some of them are my cousins.

replies.text: MAGNIFICENT! Hear that? Even the cousins! Especially the cousins!
HA! Honest! Roasted is how we love them best. Don't tell the cousins.
Away? They're family! Fine. They'll sulk. They sulk loudly.

chatter.text: A hoglin sleeps in a heap with the herd. You'd think the bottom one would complain. He never does. He's the oldest, and he likes the warmth.
I count the herd at the start of a shift and at the end. A hoglin doesn't wander off, he storms off. You can hear the gap.
I named a calf after the shiniest visitor I know. It's already biting. Nobody's surprised.

replies.text: Honoured! Ha! You should be. That calf has the best bite in the pen. Come back and I'll show you the scar.
Too late. It answers to the name now. Well, it bites when I say it. Same thing.

chatter.text: Wild hoglins get meaner as they grow older. The old ones know every trick. I respect them. Then I shoot them.
Old Grumblesnout led my herd for eleven Counts and never once let me through the gate without a fight. When he went, the pen stayed silent a whole sleep. I miss being bitten by him.
At the Great Count the whole Hold counts the Hoard together. Every nugget, every Piglin shouting the number. It takes ages. Best part of living here.
When the war horn blows everyone shouts back at it. Nobody remembers why. We just do. The horn seems to like it.
Longhouse rules: one fire, one pot, one snoring contest. Whoever loses sleeps by the door.
The barter ring has one rule: you can't take back a shout. Say 'two ingots' and it's two ingots, even if you meant nuggets. Ask {neighbour}.
Every Hold has a tune the horn plays when the Brutes change places. Three notes. We hum it when we're nervous. I'm humming it now.
In the {clan} we name babies after the loudest thing they do in their first sleep. My name is half a sneeze.
The {clan} don't forgive and don't forget. But we do lend. With interest. And a loud reminder.

replies.text: Half again, and a loud thank-you. The thank-you's the costly part.
BORROW? From the {clan}? You haven't earned the right to owe us yet. Come back when you're shinier.

chatter.text: The {clan} have a saying: the Hoard forgives, the Brute doesn't. We say it so the young ones don't test either.
The oldest in the {clan} says our tusks came from the first hoglin ever bitten. I think he made it up. I also think it's true.
Tusk-clash: two Piglins press helmets and shove till one gives. I've yielded twice. In my defence, both times it was a Brute.
Shouting contest at the ring: whoever's still loud when the rest are hoarse wins. I won with a whisper once. Nobody could argue. They'd lost their voices.
Want to try a tusk-clash? I'll be gentle. I won't be, but I'll say it.

replies.text: HA! Helmets on! ...Ow! Good! Again!
WOULD YOU! Say it again, but closer, so I can hit you!
Fair. Come when you've eaten. I like a fed opponent.

chatter.text: A nugget buys a meal. An ingot buys a bargain. A block buys a favour. The whole Hoard buys the right to shout at everybody.
Every Hold presses its mark into its ingots. Ours is a tusk with three notches. Fake the mark and your snout goes in the mould.
The pedestal in the ring has a groove worn by a hundred thousand ingots. Stand in it and you feel lucky. I do. Then I check my pockets.
Hoard counted. Eleven times. Same every time. Good.
Tower high. Lava far. Fine view.
Hoglins respect me. Piglins fear me. Children climb me. Hrm. Fair.

replies.text: Hrm. ...Maybe. A little. Don't tell.

chatter.text: I touched the Hoard gate and the Brute looked at me. I touched it again. He looked again. We did it for ages. I think I won.
Baby hoglins are my best friends. They bite, but they squeal after. That's polite.
I can shout louder than {neighbour}! I tried! They said stop, but stop means I won.
I tried tusk-clash with a baby hoglin and lost. It's not fair. It has a hard head!
When I'm big I'm going to sit on top of the horn tower and shout at the lava.

replies.text: It will! It'll shout back! ...Blorp! Like that!
Brutes don't fall. I'll be a Brute. Brutes don't fall. It's the rule.

chatter.text: A Withren once stood in my doorway and looked at me. Just looked. For ages. I've never felt so counted.
The Withren put your name on a wall when you die. We put your gold in a pot. Fair enough. I know which I'd rather have.
Soul fire gives me a headache behind the tusks. The Withren light their lanes with it on purpose. On purpose! They want us to stay away.
A Withren told a Wanderer that his armour would make a lovely memorial. Said it flat. Nobody knows if it was a joke. The Wanderer left early.
They say a Withren keeps one dead person in their head, forever. Imagine remembering that much. I can't remember where I buried my second-best nugget.
I once found a Withren child lost in the soul sand. I led it to the edge, said nothing, and ran. I still think about its face. Hush. I never said that.
Ever met a Withren up close? I haven't. I've only seen them standing far off, looking.

replies.text: Quiet, not cruel. Hm. Quiet's worse, you can't hear them coming. ...But fair. Don't repeat that.
AFRAID? CAUTIOUS! There's a difference! Ask my axe! ...My axe agrees!
A tall shape, a pale glow, and a lot of staring. Then nothing. I slept with my axe for three sleeps.

chatter.text: My grandsire said a Magmari ferryman haggled him down on a price already agreed, then charged him for the haggling. The family's still angry. We admire it.
Imagine standing in lava and complaining you're cold. That's a Magmari. I'd laugh if they didn't have longer arms than me.
Gold melts on a Magmari's skin, so they can't be rich, can't have rank, can't shake on a deal. How do they trust each other? They haggle. Huh. That's a handshake of sorts.
The fastest thing a strider does is shiver. I've timed it. I'm not saying how.
A strider shivers when it's out of the lava. Little sad shivers. I gave one a warm fungus once. It looked at me like I'd handed it a crown.
Ever ridden a strider? I'd like to know what it's like. Don't tell anyone I asked.

replies.text: Warm! Smooth! ...I'm picturing it. Don't look at me. I'm picturing it.
Me? On a Magmari's cattle? With the Magmari watching? ...Let me think about it. Let me think a lot.
My boots are hoglin hide. They'd laugh at the lava. ...Probably.

chatter.text: The Wither burned the Moorings too. I heard the Magmari hang the burned chain-links on their hearth posts. We keep burned bricks. We're not so different. Don't tell them.
I watched a Weft thread a needle with one hand, hold a net with another and scratch an ear with a third. A fourth hand did nothing. Showing off.
Weft silk is the finest cloth in the Nether. Don't tell them I said so. They'd click at me, all proud.
A Weft net caught me by the ankle once. They looked, clicked, wove something into their cloth, and cut me down. I'm in a cloth somewhere. Upside down.
They say the Long Cloth keeps every Piglin who ever fought them. I want a good row. Mine would read 'Shouted. Won.' Short. True.
A Silkgrub is a fat teal grub with glowing orange spots. I asked a Weft if I could roast one. The click they made! I haven't been that scared since a Brute smiled at me.

replies.text: Let me! They clicked so hard a net fell! No roast. I asked nicely and they said no nicely, and that's worse.

chatter.text: The Weft shear their grubs for string and the grubs look pleased about it. I never saw anything so fat and so calm. I envy it.
The Weft click when they think. I tried. *click click* Hear it? Terrible. I need practice.

replies.text: PERFECT? Flatterer! Keep flattering. I'm not stopping you.
Teach you? *click* Like that. No, with the teeth. *click* ...Stop. You're better than me. Stop it.
Stop? It's culture! *click click* ...It's culture.

chatter.text: I shot at a Ghastkin once, thinking it was a ghast whelp. It cried on my arm. The cut closed. I forgot why I was angry. I haven't told anyone.
The Ghastkin cry for everybody's dead. Even a Piglin's. I'd never ask. But if they cried for me I... wouldn't mind.

replies.text: You? ...Hm. Hm. Shiny-eyed, are you? Come here. No, stay there. Good.
True. That's the odd thing about them. They don't pick. ...I'd like to be picked. Forget I said that.

chatter.text: The ghasts scream like it hurts, because it does, they say. They were people once. I shout back less when I think about it. A little less.
There's a floaty bell-thing the Ghastkin lead on a rope. I watched a ghast turn away from it. A ghast! It went quiet and drifted off. I sat down. I couldn't tell you why.
An Ashbell rings so faintly you feel it in your teeth. I leaned in to hear. The Ghastkin looked at me. I said I was looking for gold. They believed me.
The Ghastkin float. I hate it. If you're going to be above me, be above me honestly, on a tower, with a horn.
A Cairnback carries a fire on its back that isn't proper fire. Blue. I hit one with my axe once. The axe bounced. I apologised to the axe.
The Withren walk their Cairnbacks in a line, slow as grief. I watched one pass. I felt I should take my helmet off. I didn't. But I wanted to.
A Cairnback is a rock that walks, with a small fire on top. I want one for the Hoard gate. Nothing gets past a rock with a fire.
Floaty. Pale. Crossbows up. Always. Hrm.
Long arms in the trees. Four. Count twice. Hrm.
Is it true the Weft climb with all four arms at once? I can only climb with two and a half. The half is my teeth.
I saw a pale floaty person cry once, and I cried too! Then I said I didn't. Don't tell.
Grown-ups say gold melts on Magmari. I tried melting a nugget on my tongue. It was bad. I still don't know about Magmari.
Your armour has a dent on the left side. A hoglin? Tell me it was a hoglin.

replies.text: A HOGLIN! Of course it was! Tell me all of it. Slowly. With the noises.
A fall. Hm. The lava is patient but the floor is cruel. Fair enough.
Everything is my business! ...Fine. Keep your dent.

chatter.text: You walk with your knees a little bent, like you expect the floor to leave. Wise. It does that here.
Your boots are quiet. A Piglin's boots should be loud. Loud boots say I'm here, I'm armed, I'm shouting. Yours say hm.
You smell like somewhere else. Not Rotted, not ash. Something green and cool. I like it and I don't.
You haven't boasted once since you got here. Not even a little. How do you live? How does anything get done?

replies.text: Speaks! Gold speaks. Axes speak. Work mumbles. ...But I see what you mean. Almost.

replies.ask: I could boast, if you like.
replies.text: THEN DO IT! Shoulders back, tell me how great you are! I'll wait! I'll cheer!

chatter.text: Your gold hums a low note when you move. Honest gold hums. Cheap gold squeaks. You have good taste, or good luck. Either's fine by me.
Gold on you and not a scratch on the gold. You avoid fights or you win them. Both are fine. Only one makes a good story.
You keep looking over your shoulder. Good. A Piglin who stops looking over his shoulder is a Rotted waiting to happen.
I know your walk now. I hear you coming from the next longhouse and tell the others it's the shiny one. They stop swinging early.
I carved your name in the beam over my bench. Small letters. You earned small letters. They'll grow.
You've been staring at my axe for ages. The axe is fine, thank you. Ask about something else.
No gold, and you walk about my Hold like you own it. I like that. Don't let the others see I like it.
Bare of gold you look thinner, and kinder somehow. Odd. A Piglin shouldn't look kinder. I'll get used to it.
No gold, and you came to see me anyway. That's trust. Or you forgot. Tell me it's trust.

replies.text: TRUST! Hear it? ...Now put some gold on before you leave this room. Trust has limits. The limits are the others.
Forgot! Ha! A friend who forgets his gold forgets his fear. Dangerous. Wonderful. Put it on.

chatter.text: They say the ground in your world is soft and grows green fur. Fur! On the GROUND! Does it bite?

replies.text: Grass! A word like a sneeze. Grass. GRASS! ...And you walk on it? On purpose?
Soft! To sleep on! ...I'd never wake up. I'd miss my snoring neighbours. Hm. Maybe I wouldn't.

chatter.text: Is it true your world's roof is blue and goes up forever? Nothing to bounce a shout off? What do you DO?

replies.text: Shout anyway! Into NOTHING! That's the bravest thing I ever heard.

chatter.text: They say your world has no lava anywhere. Where do you put things you want gone? Do you just keep them? Forever?
Do Overworld folk have gold? If they do, why don't they wear it? What are they doing with it?

replies.text: BURY it? Underground? Lonely gold! I'll weep. I'm weeping. It's the heat.
Food! Hm. Sensible. Disgusting, but sensible.

chatter.text: I stood at a portal once. Purple, humming, pulling at my snout. I put one foot forward. Then I put it back. That's all I did, and I call it brave.
Does it hurt, coming through? From your world to ours? Or only going out?
If my mind ever goes soft and slow like the Rotted, don't spare me. Hit me, loudly, and say my name. I'd rather go with a shout than a shuffle.

replies.text: THAT is what I want. Name and noise. I'll sleep easier knowing it.
Pah. Probably not. Say the name anyway. Practise it.

chatter.text: I dream of the three-headed thing sometimes. Always the same: somebody shouts and nobody answers. I wake up shouting. Everyone's used to it.
A golden apple! In MY Hold! If you eat it, I will cry. If you give it to me, I will cry louder.
You've got a clock in that pack, haven't you? Gold, round, spins like it's drunk in here. Show me. Don't show me. Show me.
A crossbow on your back! Good. Do you shoot it, or carry it to look dangerous? Both work. I do both.
You've got soul fire on you. Blue. Put it away before my bristles stand up.
Pearls in your pack. I know that hum. Pearls and gold are cousins. I'd trade for one. Name your price. No. Name three prices.
Iron in your pack. I can smell the dullness. Keep it in there. Away from me.
I've been studying your armour since you walked in. Who riveted it? Four rivets at the shoulder. Brave maker. Or lazy.
I tracked you in from the bridge. Clean, even prints. Nobody else walks that carefully. Hunters notice. Hunters also remember.
You walk loud. Good. Quiet ones are thieves.
Know your step now. Heard you from the gate. Hrm.
You're the shiny one, aren't you? You look like gold walking! Can I walk behind you? I'll be your shadow. Shadows don't ask for nuggets.
Your helmet is so big! Does it fall over your eyes? Mine does. Mother says grow into it.
Are you from the rotting world? You don't look rotten. You look nice. Is it nice there?

replies.text: Nice! With gold? ...No gold? Then it's NOT nice. But thank you for saying.

chatter.text: The Gilded Stair is the only step in the Bastion that still shines. We polish it with our boots. Anyone else takes the long way round.
The throne room has no throne. We sit on the floor where it stood, in a circle, and argue about who should have had it.
In the central hall the fire ate the ceiling. The glow comes straight down from the lava. I call it a skylight. It lights my bench nicely.
Sometimes the vault door groans, a low sound, like the Hoard turning over in its sleep. The Brutes don't flinch. I do. Quietly.
Melted gold runs through the cracks of the east wall like veins. Pretty. Don't pick at it. {neighbour} did, a slab fell, and now we have a new window.
The old banners hang in rags down the Long Hall. Some are mine. Some are my grandsire's. The fire took the colour. We kept the cloth.
Scavengers come down for the gold. Big talkers, small hands. We let them look at the first wall. After that, the Brutes decide.

replies.ask: Do any get past the Brutes?
replies.text: Past? Ha! Not past. Through, sometimes. In pieces. We sweep up after.
Good. Say it again when you've had time to look at the gold. Honest folk say it twice.
A little! A LITTLE! Hear that, Brutes? Out! No. Stay. But keep your hands in sight. Both of them.

chatter.text: I know every hole in the floor by heart. New ones don't open, they get found by whoever falls in. Last time it was {neighbour}. The hole bears their name now.
The stone in the warm rooms is still hot from the old fire. We take turns. I'm next. I'm always next. I've been next for ages.
Sometimes a ghast floats past the broken wall and looks in. We look out. We both pretend not to see. It's the politest thing in the Bastion.
There's a gold door in the lower halls that opens onto solid stone. Nobody's tried it since the fire. I have a theory. It's not a good theory. It's loud.

replies.text: That there's more gold behind it. Told you. Loud. Not good. But loud.
Shut. Yes. Some doors know why they're shut. Wise. Annoying, but wise.

chatter.text: Sometimes the walls tick like they're cooling. I like to think it's the old Piglins, counting. I count along. Quietly. Don't tell.
I've slept in nine Holds and one hoglin pen. The pen was warmer. The Hold was safer. The pen had better conversation.
I measure the Nether in bridges. That road has four. That one has eleven and two are lies.
I eat what I find and boast about what I don't. Lately it's mostly fungus and boasting.
A lone Piglin sleeps in short pieces. Hands on the gold, eyes on the lava. Dreams come in bites.
Every Hold wants a Wanderer's news and nobody wants a Wanderer's company. You're the sort who stays to talk. I notice.

replies.text: ...Hm. So am I. Keep that quiet.
Hard, yes. Also free. Also quiet, in the good way. Sometimes. Not often. Sometimes.

chatter.text: Out here I mark my way with a nugget wedged in a crack. Then someone takes the nugget. Then I'm lost. Then I have a story.
Ghasts own the open air. The crimson owns the ground. I own whatever's in my pack. Everybody's got a claim.
A golden sword is too soft for a real fight and too lovely to leave at home. So I carry it and shout. Works nine times in ten.
A crossbow wants three things: a steady hand, a steady heart and steady arrows. I've got two. Guess which one is missing.
My axe is called Honest. It never lies about what it's about to do.
Gold armour doesn't stop a blade like iron. It stops the thought before the blade. No Piglin swings at gold. That's the real armour.
Fix a dent with a hammer, a curse and a loud word. The curse is optional. The loud word isn't.
A helmet is where a Piglin keeps his pride. Nuggets in the lining, notches on the rim. Mine has nine notches. Nine fights. Eight won.
Sword or crossbow? Think. Your answer shows your whole character.

replies.text: Honest! Close and honest. The Brutes will like you. Then they'll try you.
Safe! Hm. Clever. Cowardly. Clever. Both. I'll allow it.
BOTH AND A LOUD VOICE! The correct answer! Say it again! Say it louder!

chatter.text: Piglins sleep in heaps, like hoglins. Warm, loud, itchy. Nobody wants to sleep alone in the Nether. Alone is for the Withren.
I dream of gold mostly. Rivers of it. In the best dreams I'm in the river and nothing's wet. Lovely. I wake up angry.
I fall asleep counting and wake up recounting. Some sleeps I'm up three nuggets. Some I'm down two. It's a hard life.
The lava seas hum when the heat's high. Stand near and listen and you can hear them thinking. Slowly. Mostly about us.
I like the glow on the ceiling. Makes everything look like gold. Even {neighbour}. Especially {neighbour}, who needs the help.
Vault door closed. Me beside it. Right order. Hrm.
Burned walls. Strong walls. Me inside. Hrm.
Wind in the cracks. Sounds like thieves. Is wind. Hrm.
Shh. I know where the loose stone is. It's my secret hole. And my secret nugget under my secret hole.
When I can't sleep I count nuggets. I always fall asleep at four. Four is a very sleepy number.
I'm going to be a Wanderer and see ALL the Holds and take all the gold! Hm. No. Ask for it. Nicely. Loud-nicely.

replies.text: It IS exciting! I'll bring you a nugget from every Hold! If I find any! If I don't eat them!
Nicely! Loud-nicely! ...PLEASE GIVE ME YOUR GOLD! Like that? Was that nice?

chatter.text: Mother says don't talk to strangers with gold. But you're gold. So you're a stranger and a friend. That's confusing. Do you have a nugget?
You're my favourite grown-up! I have a list. You're at the top. Above Mother. Don't tell Mother.
I told everyone you can beat a Brute. Can you? Please say you can. I bet three nuggets.

replies.text: EASILY! I knew it! I'm RICH! Wait for me here, I'm going to tell them!
Aww. I'll still say you can. I already bet.

chatter.text: I lost a baby tusk! Mother put it in the Hoard. A tiny bit of me is in the Hoard now. I'm practically rich!
I practised being a Brute. I stood very still, frowned, and said hrm. Nobody noticed. Maybe I'm a good Brute.

replies.text: HRM! HRM! You did it too! We're a Brute club! Hrm!

chatter.text: The horn is so loud I feel it in my feet. Do your feet go wobble too? Mine do. It tickles.
I'm not allowed up the horn tower. I'm allowed on the first step. So I live on the first step. It's a very good step.
I found the tip of a hoglin's tusk on the floor. Is it mine now? If I find it, it's mine. That's the rule.
I'm playing Hoard. I'm the Hoard. You have to guard me. Don't let anyone take me! ...Brute! Don't take me!

replies.text: YES! Guard me forever! ...Unless there are snacks.

chatter.text: Guess what! I climbed the pens and didn't fall in! I fell out. Out is better than in.
I know all the songs! Well, I know the loud part of all the songs. That's the best part.
I kept my shiniest pebble back for you. It's nearly a nugget. It's a bit licked. Not by me. Mostly by me.

replies.text: I'll keep it safe in my mouth! No. In my pocket. Under the bench. ...Both.
Oh. Fine. I'll eat it. I mean keep it. I mean... I'll keep it.

chatter.text: When I grow up I want to guard you. Like a Brute, but nicer. Brutes are never nice. I'll be nice-and-big.
Grown-ups say don't beg. I'm not begging. I'm asking with my whole face.
Do you have a pet? I have a pebble. It's a very good pet. It never bites. It never does anything. It's perfect.

replies.text: Other Gold! Because Gold was the other pebble. Gold ran off. Pebbles do that. Other Gold stays.
BORING? He's SHY! You hurt his feelings! Say sorry to him. Say it nicely.

chatter.text: I tried to count the sparks on the ceiling and ran out of numbers at nine. Then I started again. Then I ran out again.
Why is the Brute always angry? I asked. He said hrm. I asked again. He said hrm. I think that's his whole angry.
Mother let me hold the horn! It was heavy! It made a big noise! I got in trouble. It was the best trouble.
Do you think I'll get rich? Mother says wait. Father says work. {neighbour} says be born a Brute. I say can I have a nugget?
My litter is six and loud. Six! Each louder than the last. My ears will never recover. My heart is full. Both true.
I've got a son who bites. I bite back. That's fatherhood. The rest is shouting.
When I was small my mother sang the counting song, slow, so I'd sleep. I do it for mine now. I'm terribly off-key. I do it anyway.
My father said a good shout starts in the heels and climbs. Throat-shouters wear out early. I'm all heels. I'm never hoarse.
Raising a Piglin is easy. You feed it, shout at it, and pretend not to love it. That last part is the hard bit.

replies.text: ...I might. Don't shout it. Well. Shout it a little.

chatter.text: Watch the little ones near the pens. They think hoglins are friends. Hoglins think little ones are snacks. Both are right.

replies.ask: I'll keep an eye on them.
replies.text: Good! A shiny one watching the little ones! I'll tell the Brutes to leave you be while you do.
They do. Mostly roasted. Keep that away from the little ones.

chatter.text: Every litter has one that doesn't shout. A quiet one. We love the quiet ones best. Shh. That's a secret.

replies.text: ...Were you? Come here. Sit. Loud is easy. Quiet takes more. I'll say it quietly.
Loud IS easier. That's why they need the love.

chatter.text: The {clan} babies are born biting. Fair warning if you ever hold one.
Traders come in three kinds: those who shout, those who sulk and those who lie. The liars pay best.
Someone traded me an ingot for a single gravel and thanked me. I'm still afraid he knew something I didn't.
The crimson woods are quiet if you don't listen. If you listen, every leaf is a hoglin. Don't listen too hard.
My crossbow is called Nine Steps. That's how far a hoglin gets after a good shot. After a bad shot it's called Ten Steps. And I run.
I know where the best quartz sits and who's fighting over it. Quartz fights are the worst. Quartz doesn't even shine properly.
Warped fungus in my basket? Never. I wash my hands after touching it. The herder smells it anyway and glares.
I read furnace flame like a face. Orange is happy. White is angry. Blue is somebody's idea of a joke, and I leave.
First thing I learned at the forge: gold forgives. Bend it wrong, bend it back. Iron never forgives. Never apologises, either.
Small one sleeps on my boots. Won't move. Hrm. Hold still, boots.
Hoard path: walk it slow. Fast feet look guilty. Hrm.
I never learned to count past a hundred. I fake it. At every Hoard count I shout a big number and nobody checks. You're the first I've told. Don't check me.
I'm afraid of the high bridges. I shut my eyes and shout. Everyone thinks it's a battle cry.
I slip the hoglins extra fungus and tell nobody. The herder thinks they're fat from luck. They're fat from me. I'm thin from guilt.
Once I let a thief go. A small one, from another Hold, hungry. I looked the other way. If the Brutes knew... Well. Now you know. You're a vault.
I never told anyone my real fear. It's not the Wither. It's not the Rotted. It's being the last one shouting in an empty Hold.

replies.text: You... would. I believe you. ...Good. That's one. One's enough to start a Hold.
Maybe not. Hm. Say it anyway, loud enough to scare the quiet off.

chatter.text: Tusk-kin. We say it at births, not for gold. You know that? Gold is for friends. Tusks are for blood. You're blood now.
When I'm old and slow, come and sit by me and tell me the old fights, even if I can't remember them. Promise? Loud promise.

replies.text: THAT'S A PROMISE! Everyone heard it! Now you can't take it back!
Ha! Flatterer. Everybody's slow in the end. But thank you. I'll be quick as long as I can.

chatter.text: My mother's helmet hangs on my wall. She never took it off for anything. I put it on once and cried. Don't tell.
My old shield-mate fell off a bridge ten steps from me. I still hear the shout he made. Loud and rude. I hope that's the last thing the lava heard.
You walk bare through the Hold and nobody swings. I've been watching your back the whole time. That's what a friend does. It's tiring.
I rarely talk this long. Usually I'm shouting at somebody. Is this strange? It's like shouting, only softer, and you don't get hoarse.
If you ever need somewhere to hide, I know three. One under the forge. One in the pens behind the oldest hoglin. One I won't tell even you.

replies.text: Good. Remember the pens first. Hoglins make good doors.
Ha! Ask me when the horn blows twice. Not before.

chatter.text: When the horn blows, look for me. I'll be at the front. Looking for you is all I'll do. Then I'll fight.
They sing a song about you in the longhouse now. It's terrible. The words rhyme badly. I helped write it.

replies.text: *clears throat* Ahem. ...No, I can't. I'll cry. Later. After everyone's gone. Then I'll sing it twice.
Too late! It's already everywhere! Brace yourself, shiny!

chatter.text: Between us: the ring gives better gifts if I bang the pedestal three times. It's nonsense. But the barter goes well. So I bang it every time.
I've never missed a hoglin I didn't shout at first. The ones I shouted at, I missed. Let that teach the shouters. I am a shouter.
I hide a patch of the best crimson fungus where nobody goes. When I'm old, that's my feast. Now you know. Don't eat it.
My hands remember every burn. Left thumb: my first ingot. Right palm: my first bad pour. Wrist: {neighbour}'s fault. I'm proud of every scar.
I made one helmet for myself. It's perfect. I've never worn it. I look at it. That's the best part of the work: the pieces you never use.
The calves know my smell from the moment they're born. They run to my boots. Hoglins don't love like we do. They just run toward you. It's enough.
They say I could stay in any Hold I like. I never do. If I stayed I'd have to belong. Belonging is heavy. Here, with you, it's lighter.
The Bastion's burned and half gone and I'll die in it. Not soon. But I'd like it to be with the glow on the ceiling. That's all I want.
Brute has no friend. Brute has you. Hrm. That's one.
Axe is heavy. Not the axe. The waiting. Hrm.
Tusk-kin. Hrm. My shift ends when you're safe.
I wish you lived here. Then I could see you every sleep and show you every thing I've got.

replies.ask: I'll visit as often as I can.
replies.text: Promise? Loud promise? ...You didn't say it loud. Say it loud!

chatter.text: You're not scary like the other big shiny ones. You're warm-big. Warm-big is the best kind.
Mother says you're family now. Does that mean you have to come to the shouting contests? You do. I'm the loudest. I'll show you.
I'm going to give you my best pebble when I'm old enough to give things away. I'm not old enough yet. Soon. Don't forget.
I used to wear my gold to look rich. Now I wear it so you'll know me in a crowd. Small difference. Big difference.
When I'm sad I eat. When I'm happy I eat. When I'm angry I eat. I'm not sure the eating helps. But sad is quieter with a full mouth.
The others think I'm the toughest Piglin in the Hold. I let them. It's easier than saying I'd rather feed baby hoglins than fight.
I wonder sometimes if we should have kept the peace. Not with all of them. With one. Any one. Just to see if it could be done.

replies.text: ...Could it? Hm. Say that when the horn's quiet. Then I'll listen properly.
Hm. Maybe not. But I wondered. Wondering isn't a crime. Yet.

chatter.text: I used to hate the Withren with my whole chest. Now I hate them with half. The other half is curious. That half doesn't get a vote.

replies.text: Is it? Hm. Don't tell the other half. It'll start a fight.
Because of the fire. Because of the bastions. Because my grandsire hated them. Those are three good reasons. They aren't all good reasons.

chatter.text: I told my young about you. Not the gold. The shout. How you stood your ground. That's what I want them to learn.
The barter ring is so loud I can't stand it, and I love it. So I sit under the pedestal, where it's loud and quiet both. Don't tell.
{neighbour} lost a bet and has to carry a hoglin calf round the ring three times, shouting that they're a calf. They shout well. Too well.
{neighbour} says the lava seas are creeping closer. They say it every few sleeps. They're right once in a while, which is how they keep their name for wisdom.
I swapped places with {neighbour} for a shift. Now we both know why the other one is tired. We're not speaking of it.
To know a Piglin, watch how they hold a nugget. {neighbour} holds it like a sleeping calf. I hold it like a grudge.
The hearth in the longhouse never goes out. Somebody has the last watch, and nobody admits to falling asleep on it. The hearth knows.
{neighbour} owns the finest boots in the Hold and won't say where they got them. I'm following them to find out. They've noticed. We're both pretending.
{neighbour} asked about you. I said you're slow to boast and quick to listen. They said that's not a Piglin. I said that's why you're interesting.
A cold porkchop is a sad thing. Warm it against your helmet if you must. Nobody will know. Everybody will know.
Hoglin broth with fungus caps is the cure for aching bones. It tastes of heat and old fights.
Cooking over lava is quick but bitter. Cooking over a hearth is slow and fair. I like fair. So do my eyebrows.
A pinch of ash on a roast is what the oldest Piglins swear by. Tastes like regret. Tastes wonderful.
The vents hiss at certain times and we've learned to cook by them. When they hiss, the pot is ready. When they scream, run.
When the lava swells the whole Hold glows orange and we all sweat gold. Nobody complains. We boast about who sweats most.
Some say the Nether is getting hotter. They say it every few sleeps. I say it's the same heat, just closer to my face.
Oldest saying in the Hold: a quiet Hoard is a stolen Hoard. So we shout the numbers every sleep, and the thieves hear that we're counting.

replies.text: A quiet Piglin is a sulking Piglin. Same saying, different pocket. Ha!
It is. That's why we sleep so hard.

chatter.text: A dull nugget is still a nugget. A dull friend is still a friend. A dull Brute is... don't say it. He's near.
Hoglins don't lie. They just bite. I like them better than most Piglins.
Gold doesn't ask where you've been. That's why we love it. Friends ask. Gold just sits there and shines.
A Piglin who shares his stew once is generous. Twice, suspicious. Three times, in love. I've shared four times with {neighbour}. They've started saving me a spoon.
What do you call a Piglin with no gold? A guest of the Brutes. Ha! You don't have to laugh. It's mostly true.

replies.text: HA! You laughed! Do it again! I'll tell it again!
Not funny? It's a TRUE joke. True jokes aren't funny, they're accurate.

chatter.text: A Brute, a Bartermaster and a Wanderer reach a broken bridge. The Brute says hrm. The Bartermaster says how much? The Wanderer says I've heard this one. That's the whole joke.
Hoglin calves play-fight with their heads. Bonk, bonk, bonk. You can hear it across the pens. Best noise in the Nether after a spitting porkchop.
