I saw a hoglin that went through a portal and came back wrong. Green, slow, no temper. It didn't even bite me. That was the worst part.
A strider hums when it's content, low, like a pot about to boil. I heard one once. I'd have stayed longer if its owner hadn't been watching me.
The oldest hoglin in my pen has the warmest spot by the vent and nobody argues. He earned it by sitting there longer than I've been alive.
Wild hoglins hide flat and still in the crimson stems. You pass. They don't. They wait for the Piglin behind you. That's why I never walk last.
Shroomlights hang in the canopy like lamps. I take only the lowest one. The Weft call that courtesy. I call it laziness. Both are true.
Never smelt gold with bad news in your head. The metal knows. It comes out dull. I hum the horn tune the whole time.
Gilded blackstone is a rock with ambitions. I love it. It tries so hard.
A hoglin-owner bargains with his elbows. I bargain with my voice. Elbows win more often.
Free news, since you're shiny: the east road has a bridge out. Don't walk it. I'll remember I told you when we bargain.
Gold's on. Good. Eyes up, hands in sight, voice low. A shiny stranger is only as safe as his manners.
I'm still deciding about you. Take your time being likeable. I'm patient. Not very. But I'll pretend.
People wear gold for many reasons. I haven't decided yours. Keep quiet while I decide.
Armour needs oil. Oil needs time. Time needs patience. Patience, I have. Hrm.
Horn tower: three steps up, three steps down. Every shift. Good steps. Hrm.
Not a talker. A listener. Hear everything. Say nothing. Hrm.
I tried to teach a hoglin to count. It ate the counting stones. Hoglins don't like numbers. Mother says that's not the reason but I like it.
My best friend is {neighbour}'s little one. We fight every time we play. That's how you know.
I'm not afraid of the vents. They just burp. Everyone burps. It's polite to burp back.
I want a hoard under my bench. A small one. A starter hoard. Right now it's a pebble. Soon it's a nugget.
The Brute on the horn winked at me! Or something got in his eye. I'm telling everyone it was a wink.
That fungus is a good one. Crimson. Fresh. Fat. Hoglins would fight for it. So would I. Is it a gift? Don't answer. I'll stand here being tempted.
Warped fungus in your pack. I can smell it. Don't take it near the pens. The herder will bite your ankles. I'll hold him back. Slightly.
A shroomlight! Did the Weft drop a net on you for that? Show me your ankle and I'll show you mine.

lines.text: I am {name} {clan}! Say it back. Louder. Good. Now you'll remember it.
{name} of the {clan}. Best clan in the Nether. Every clan says that. We say it loudest, so we win.
The {clan} name is older than the fire. We lost the bastions, the gold, half our tusks. We kept the name. Names don't melt.
I'm {name}, {job}, of the {clan}. And you're the pink-skin who wears gold. What are you to us?

replies.text: Ha! Bold. I like bold. Keep saying it until it's true.
Nobody just passes through wearing gold. Gold always means something.
Nobody special doesn't wear gold. Stand up straight. You're shaming your helmet.

lines.text: Between us? My grandsire won the {clan} name in a bet. Still counts. A bet is a bet. Don't tell the clan.
{name}. {clan}. Brute. Enough.
My mother named me for the first noise I made. {name}. She says it was a roar. My sister says it was a burp. Nobody can prove it.
Six in my litter and one trough. That's where I learned to shout. If you don't shout, you don't eat.
A short name is a good name. It fits in a shout. A long name falls over halfway across the lava. Mine is {name}. See? Still standing.
Hit one of the {clan} and the whole longhouse comes. Steal a hoglin and the whole Hold comes. Do both and we send for the cousins.
I'm {name}, Bartermaster. Ask anyone. They'll say I'm fair. Then they'll check their pockets. That's how you know I'm good.
I'm {name}. I find the meat. Be nice to me and the meat finds you. Be rude and you eat fungus. Warped fungus.
{name}, Forager. I know every glowing thing in the crimson by name. I even know the ones that bite. Those I know best.
I'm {name}, Smelter. The heat took my eyebrows and my manners. It left my voice. That's the part I use.
{name}, Goldsmith. Every shiny thing on every Piglin in this Hold passed through my hands first. You're welcome. Say it. You're welcome.
{name}, Hoglin-herder. The pens know my voice, the herd knows my smell, and my ears know my herd's teeth. Ask me about my ears.
{name} of the {clan}, Wanderer. A Piglin without a Hold is still a Piglin. Just louder, and with a lot more walking.
{name}, of the Bastion. My family's been in these halls since before the fire. We were here when it came. We were here after. We'll be here.
I'm the one who laughs last in the {clan}. Not because I'm slow. Because I wait for the right moment, and then I'm very, very loud.
Odd, telling a pink-skin my name and meaning it every time. You've turned me soft. Don't tell {neighbour}. I'd have to hit you in public.
Here's a thing I don't say. I wanted to be a Brute. Too small, too chatty. So I became this. Turns out the Hold needs loud ones too.
Who am I? The one who'd hand you the last ingot in the Nether and complain about it for a year. Worth every complaint, Tusk-kin.
My father filed my tusks flat in my tenth year. I screamed the whole time. That's tradition. Screaming is half of tradition.
Ask who holds the purse in the {clan}. They point at me, then my mother, then her mother. The women of this clan don't lose arguments.
You asked who I am. Now tell me. Am I important?

replies.text: THE MOST! Say it to {neighbour}. Say it loud. I'll hold your gold while you do.
Enough! Hm. Enough is a bit small. But it's a start. We'll grow it.
Bigger? BIGGER? Name one. No, don't. I'll go and fight them.

lines.text: Born in a Hold, living on the road. A name, a clan and a pocketful of gold. That's all a Piglin needs to be somebody.
Every one of the {clan} gets a nickname from the first thing they break. Mine was a helmet. Not even mine. Ask me the rest when we're better friends.
I've been called Greedy, Loud and Rude. All true. I've also been called Fair. That one I made up. Try it on me.
I never forget who gave me gold and I never forget who took it. Two long lists. You're on the first one. For now.
Name is {name}. Mother picked it. Short. Easy to shout when I'm needed.
Who am I? The one who stands where you walk. Hrm. That's enough.
I'm {name}. Not 'Brute'. Brute is a job. {name} is me. Hrm. Remember.
Was small once. Was loud once. Gate made me quiet. Gate is fine.

lines: Gold is rank. More gold, more say. Less gold, less say. No gold, no say. Also no head.
Gold is savings. It doesn't rot, it doesn't rust, it doesn't run off. It just sits there being beautiful.
Gold is the handshake. You show gold, I show gold, nobody stabs anybody. That's peace, the Piglin way.
We first wore it in the war, so we'd know our own in the smoke. Nobody else would touch the stuff. Still true. Except you.

lines.text: First you tell me. What is gold to you?

replies.text: EVERYTHING! Yes! You understand! I knew it the moment you shone!
Trading, yes. That's the second-best thing gold does. The first is shining.
Just shiny... Out of my sight. No. Stay. I'll fix you. It'll take a while.

lines.text: A nugget is a sip. An ingot is a meal. A block is a feast. A Hoard is a whole life. Learn which one you're holding.
Listen. *tink* That's real gold. Fake gold goes thud. Pretend gold goes 'sorry'. I can hear a lie from three paces.
Gold stays warm in the hand. Iron goes cold. That's how you know which one loves you.
We seal a deal over an ingot. Both hold on. First to let go loses. Nobody's let go in sixty years. Some have lost arms.
Gold teeth! Best thing a Piglin can own. Bite a Brute with one and he remembers you. Bite a Bartermaster and he pays.
I keep a nugget under my tongue when I'm worried. Don't laugh. It's cold, then warm, then I'm fine.
My first ingot came from my father. Never melted, never spent. It's the one thing I'd never barter, not for ten pearls.
If the fire came again, I'd save the children, the Hoard and a nugget. In that order. No. Children, Hoard, you. Hrm. Maybe you before the Hoard.
Here's the truth, Tusk-kin. It was never the gold. It was someone handing you something shiny and trusting you not to run. You didn't. That's all gold is for.
What's the most gold you've ever held in your two hands?

replies.text: A WHOLE BLOCK! In your own hands! Did you cry? Be honest. I'd have cried.
A few. Honest. That's a start. A good start. Hold more, hold longer.
Give it AWAY? Why would... Hm. To who? ...Fine. That's kind. Still wrong. Kind, though.

lines.text: Pure gold is too soft to fight with. So we wear it where we don't fight: the helmet, the chest, the pride. The pride is the heaviest part.
Raw gold has a smell, like a hot nugget dipped in smoke. Once you've smelled it, you can't stop. My nose is worth more than my sword.
An ingot buys what it likes. Sometimes it likes pearls. Sometimes it likes gravel. I don't make the rules. The gold does.
I wear gold on the hunt so the other Piglins don't shoot me by mistake. Two have tried. Nice folk. Terrible aim.
Hoglins don't care about gold. It's their one flaw. They'll gore a war-chief and ignore his helmet.
I carry all of mine on my body. Pockets, belt, helmet, boots. When I walk I jingle. That's how folk know I'm coming. And how I know they're afraid.
Look at the floor. See the swirl of dull yellow in the stone? Gold that ran down the walls when the fire came. It cooled where it fell. We scrape up a little whenever we need it.
Every longhouse keeps a gold block by the hearth. It's the family's. Nobody touches it. We look at it when we argue, to remember what we're arguing for.
Never stack your gold where a Brute can see it. He counts too. Slowly. Out loud. It ruins everything.
When the fire melted the bastions, the gold ran into the cracks and set hard. We cut it out in slabs, so some of our ingots are crooked. Crooked means old.
Nether gold hides in the netherrack as little flecks. I can smell it. The trick is not to dig it up in front of a Hunter. They cry about shares.
Gold. Mine to guard. Not mine to have. Hrm. Is fine.
Gold hurts to look at. Good hurt.
Brute counts it. Alone. In my head. Never out loud. Hrm. Same number every time. Good number.
Would you ever give your gold away? Think before you answer. I'm listening with my whole face.

replies.text: For a friend. Hm. HM! That's not a Piglin answer. It's a good one, though. Ask me again when I've eaten.
Never! Good! ...Never? Not even... no. Good. Never. We agree. Stop looking at my pockets.
NOW you're a Piglin! Name your price. I'll pretend to be shocked.

lines.text: Some say gold is only something the earth did by accident. Those people have no gold.
{village}! Three longhouses, one Hoard, one horn, and the loudest barter ring this side of the lava.
The barter ring is the heart of the Hold. Gold block on the pedestal. Touch it and find out what we're like. Actually, don't.
Longhouse life: one hearth, one gold block, too many Piglins, all snoring. You get used to it. Or you go deaf. Same thing.
Climb the horn tower if you like. The Brute up top won't stop you. He'll just stare until you climb back down.
The forge is where the gold gets pretty. Don't touch the cauldron. It's lava, not soup. {neighbour} learned that one.
This was a bastion, the greatest in the Nether. Then the Wither came. Outsiders call it a Remnant now. We call it home.
See the black on the walls? Soot from the fire. We never scrubbed it off. Some things you keep where you can see them.
Our Bastion. Burned, broken, ours. What do you think of it?

replies.text: Even burned! Even burned it's better than anything up in your rotting world.
Everything needs work. You need work. Ha!
A RUIN? It's a home with a bad past. Watch your mouth this close to the lava.

lines.text: This? This is nowhere. Lava and fungus. My Hold is wherever my gold is, and my gold is on me.
Out here there's no horn to call your friends. Just me, my crossbow and my mouth. The mouth works best.
Listen at the walls. Hear the snoring? Eleven Piglins, one hoglin and a Brute who talks in his sleep. Never repeat what he says.
The Hoard has a rule: nobody sleeps within three paces of it. Everybody ignores the rule. That's why we have the Brute.
We build longhouses from crimson stems because crimson wood won't burn. Fire is the one thing we respect.
The horn tower has the best view and the worst wind. The Brute up there hasn't blinked since I was a whelp.
The pens are downwind of the longhouses. Lucky for us. Unlucky for visitors who find them by nose.
The barter ring's floor is worn smooth. Generations of boots stomping one spot. That's all a Hold is: boots wearing a hole in one place.
Every Hold has a loudest corner. Ours is outside the forge. Come and shout there. We'll tell you how you did.
Blackstone under every longhouse so the lava can't creep in. A cousin's Hold lost a whole street to it once. We talk about it at feasts. Quietly. Quietly for us.
My favourite part of {village}: when the horn blows for a feast, even the Brutes grin. Just a little. You'd miss it if you blinked.
{village} has taken in more strays than I can count. Wanderers, orphans, one very lost Hunter. We take you in, then we shout at you. It's a good life.
If you ever need a roof, there's a bench by my hearth. Not a bed. A bench. But it's mine, and it's yours. That's the biggest thing a Piglin can offer.
The elders want your name carved over the gate, between the tusk and the horn. I'd carve it deeper. {village} is yours, Tusk-kin.
What do you make of {village}? Say something kind. Or loud. Either is fine.

replies.text: Wonderful! Hear that, wall? Wonderful! Say thank you to the nice gold-wearer.
LOUD? We're being QUIET! ...Ha. You're right. Say that again. I love it.
Where? Name it. I'll go and set it on fire. Then it's even.

lines.text: The bridge to the east hall is half a bridge now. We jump the gap. The ones who miss are legends.
The stone in the lower rooms is still warm, after all this time. It remembers the fire. So do we.
My grandsire told of the Bastion when it was whole: gold on every roof, banners on every arch. I look at the cracks and try to see it. Sometimes I almost can.
We keep the old hoglin stables swept, though no hoglin sleeps in them. Habit. Also hope.
People ask if we mean to rebuild. We do. One stone at a time, gold in every mortar line. It'll be done in a hundred years. Or two.
There's a room in the east wing nobody sleeps in. The fire stopped at its door. We leave a nugget on the sill. Sometimes it's gone when we look again. We say it's rats.
Between us? We could leave. Holds would take us. We stay because this is the one place the Wither didn't win. We're still here. That's our answer.
Vault below. Walls above. Me between. Hrm. Good place.
The wastes have no walls, and I love that. You see the lava from far off. You see the Rotted from far off. You never see your friends.
Out here I sleep light and boast quiet. At a Hold I sleep heavy and boast loud. Fair trade.
There's an old gold vein in the hills near here. I won't say where. I'll say it's a long walk that way. Then I'll say I lied.
When I see you in the wastes I feel better. Funny. Alone I'm the loudest Piglin in the Nether. With you I'm the loudest of two.
Every Hold I pass asks me to stay. I always say later. Later is where I live.
Out here you eat what you find. Fungus, mostly. Last time it was my own belt. I'm not proud. It was tender.
I run the barter ring. You give gold, I give things. Which things? Whatever the gold decides. Gold has moods.
Bartermaster. I'm fair, I'm fast, and if you argue I count slower. Want a tip?

replies.text: Never show your whole purse. Show a bit, and look sad. Not with me, though. You're with me.
Ha! Everyone needs tips. That's why I'm rich and you're the one asking.

lines.text: I hunt wild hoglins in the crimson. Not the penned ones. Those are herd. Mean herd, but herd.
Crossbow, quiet feet, and a lot of shouting at the end. That's hunting. The shouting is the best part.
Fungus, wart, quartz, shroomlight. If it grows or glints out there, I bring it home and brag about it.
The best shroomlights hang in the warped canopy. The Weft drop nets on you. Worth it. Mostly. Once it wasn't.
I melt raw gold into ingots. Hot work. Good work. Smell my bristles. That's the smell of success.
The blast furnace roars, I roar back. The gold comes out shining. My eyebrows never come out at all.
I make the armour that keeps gold-wearers alive down here. Every Piglin in this Hold wears my work. You may bow a little.
Gold is soft. That's the trick. You don't fight it. You talk to it, hit it, then talk to it again.
I keep the pens. Crimson fungus in, warped fungus far away, fingers attached. That's the whole job.
Penned hoglins are herd, not game. Nobody hunts them. You want one for the fire, you ask me. Then I say no.
Guard. Gate. Gold. Three words. Good job.
Stand. Watch. Hit thieves. Don't sit.
Work? I live in a bastion the Wither burned. Staying alive in it is the work.
We sweep the ash, guard the old vault, and fight over who sleeps in the warm rooms. I always win.
I walk from Hold to Hold carrying news. News costs a nugget. That bit was free.
No Hold of my own. I sleep wherever my gold is safe. Usually on top of it.
I never choose what comes out of the ring. I toss the gold in, shout, and the ring decides. Pearls on a good throw. Gravel on a bad one. I blame the gravel on you.
Trade secret: gravel isn't bad luck. Gravel is the ring being funny. When I get gravel, I laugh. The ring likes that, and the next throw is better.
Truth: some folk I gave the best deals, I never saw again. Some I fleeced came back with a gift. That's how I learned who's worth the trouble.
A good hoglin hunt takes patience, a good wind and a good bluff. The wind is hardest. It changes sides when you're not looking.
I tracked one big boar across the whole crimson. Wore out two pairs of boots. Then I let it walk. It was too fine to eat. The Hold thinks I missed.
I'll tell you why I hunt. The Hold eats well when I come home. Every hunt is a promise. I've never broken one. That's my real hoard.
Weeping vines hang from the crimson roof. Twisting vines grow from the floor. I pull both. The trick is not to fall in the lava while reaching up. Learned that twice.
I wear a tiny shroomlight on a string. When I'm lost in the dark wastes I look at it and remember there are warmer places. The Hunters would laugh.
I've found things out there with no names. A glowing stone with a heartbeat. A fungus that hums. I'd show you, if I trusted my own route. I'll draw you a map. A bad one.
Gold melts on a low simmer and shouts on a high flame. You listen for the shout. When it goes quiet, it's done. If you hear singing, run.
The furnace is older than the Hold. We built the Hold round it. Hot all the time, so the whelps sleep on the warm wall. Smelters' children are always the loudest.
Once my furnace lit the roof. Three pelts burned, one wall fell. The elders were furious. Then they saw the gold. They never said sorry. They just stopped shouting.
A good helmet takes nine hundred blows and one good shout. Skip the shout and it dents.
A plate I made once came back to me off a dead Hunter. I knew it by the dent: my own thumbprint, left in the rim. I melted it into a ring for his family.
I've made a crown for a Piglin who never wore it, a helm for a Brute who died in it, and a bracelet for a whelp. The bracelet is the one I remember.
I count my hoglins by their grunts. Each one has its own. If one's missing, I hear the gap.
Feeding time is the loudest. Thirty hoglins, one trough, and me in the middle with a ladle. The only time I wish I were a Brute.
I cried when we had to cull the old boar. The whole Hold ate in his honour. I couldn't. I sat and listened to the pen. It was too quiet.
Watch the gate. Watch the people. Watch the people watching the gate.
Standing is hard. Everyone thinks it's easy. Try it. Not moving, not blinking. Hrm.
Once a whelp sat by my post the whole watch and told me every secret in the Hold. I never moved. I kept every one.
I keep the walls. A piece falls, I carry it back up. It falls again. I carry it again. The wall and I are old friends.
I take Wanderers in when the ghasts get restless. Nobody pays me. Nobody thanks me. But they remember. That's how word of the Bastion spreads.
The elders say I should find a Hold. I always say the walls need me. Truth: I'm waiting to hang the first banner again. I want to be here.
A Wanderer carries three things: news, gold and a good lie. Lose the lie and you're nobody.
I know the shortcuts between every Hold. Left at the burnt tree and don't look at the lava. I've lost three companions to looking.
I've a plan for old age. Find the Hold with the quietest horn, the warmest bench and the fewest questions. I've looked at eleven. None were quiet enough.
Think you could do my work?

replies.text: Easily! Ha! Take my place and I'll watch. I'll laugh. Loudly.
Honest. Good. The honest ones last longest in a Hold.
Teach you? Hm. Stand there. Hold this. Don't drop it. That's lesson one.

lines.text: Everyone in the Hold has work. Even the whelps. Especially the whelps, they break things, and a broken thing is a job for somebody.
I do my work loud so nobody can say I'm hiding. Quiet workers get accused of things.

lines: Piglins who went through to your world. They came back green, slow and gold-blind. That's what your world does to us.
Your world rots us. Everyone knows it. Somehow it doesn't rot you. Suspicious. Very suspicious.
Don't hit the Rotted. Hit one and they all come. They forgot their names. They didn't forget each other.

lines.text: You came out of the Overworld and you smell fine. How?

replies.text: Born in the rot and not rotted. Huh. Maybe it's slow. Check your ears now and then.
Tougher than a Piglin? Ha! No. But I like the nerve. Keep it.
Don't say that! Stand over there. Further. Further.

lines.text: My uncle went through a portal after gold. He came back Rotted. He still walks the wastes. I wave. He doesn't.

replies.text: Don't be sorry. Be careful. Keep your gold on and stay out of portals. Well. You came out of one.
HAPPY? He's rotting on his feet! Don't joke about the Rotted. Not to me. Not ever.

lines.text: We say a Piglin turns green in the time it takes to count to thirty. Nobody's counted. Nobody wants to.
Look at their swords. They still carry gold, but they swing it like a stick. They kept the gold and lost the reason. That's what the rot takes. The reason.
The Rotted gather near the portals. Nobody knows why. Some say they're waiting for someone to come back and fetch them. I hate that one best.
Throw a nugget at a Rotted and it doesn't even look. That's how you know they're really gone. A Piglin would kill for a nugget. Even a dead one.
My grandmother said: sleep on gold, never near a portal. A portal is a door that wants you. She was right about most things.
We teach whelps a counting rhyme: one for the gold, two for the horn, three for the portal, never go. It's silly. It works.
Some elders say the Rotted still know us. They stand at the edge of the Hold and watch the longhouses. I don't like it. I like it a little.
I left a nugget on the ridge for my uncle once. When I came back it was gone. I told myself it was a hoglin. Maybe it was.
If I turned Rotted, promise me one thing. Don't wait. Don't be sad. Tell the Hold I went out loud. With a good shout. That's all.
I'm not afraid of the Rotted anymore. I'm afraid of the quiet after. You've been through the portal and come out whole. Maybe that means something. Maybe everything.
Would you ever go through a portal again?

replies.text: If you had to. Hm. That's the only good reason. Wear your gold both ways.
Never! A sensible pink-skin at last. I'll tell the others you said it.
A good reason is how it starts for everyone. Be careful what counts as good.

lines.text: The Rotted walk in a line like a funeral. I've followed them. They go to the portal and stand. Then they turn round and walk back. Round and round.
On the road I give the Rotted a wide berth. A wide, loud berth. I sing. They don't like singing. Or they love it. Hard to tell.
A few Rotted wander the lower halls. We leave them be. They don't take anything. They just walk.
I made a golden bracelet for a Rotted once. Held it out on a stick. It walked past without a glance. I'm still angry about that bracelet.
Hoglins and the Rotted hate each other. Hoglins charge, the Rotted shuffle. The herd always wins. They don't boast about it, though. Unlike a Piglin.
I won't smelt anything that came off a Rotted. Even gold. It might still be... them. Is that stupid? It's stupid. I still won't.
A Rotted wandered into the barter ring once, holding a golden sword it had forgotten how to use. I gave it a fistful of gravel and it left happy. Best deal I ever made.
I've never seen a Rotted in the warped forest. Even rotten, they know better. Weft nets don't care whose side you're on.
Rotted. No gold sense. No gate sense. No sense. Hrm.
My brother went through the portal. I stood at the gate. He came back Rotted. I still stand at the gate. In case he knows it.
Rule of the Hold: if a Rotted comes near, wave. Don't shout, don't throw. Wave. It costs nothing and keeps the peace. Then go inside and shout all you like.
Do you know what scares me about the Rotted? Their eyes. The same eyes. Same colour, same shape. Just nobody in them.
Your world sees a Rotted and runs. I would too. But I'd remember it had a mother, a name and a favourite hoglin. They all did.
They never age. Rotted from my grandsire's time still shuffle the wastes. Same swords. Same shuffle. Maybe rot is a kind of forever. I don't want forever. I want a good ending.

lines: There was gold under the soul valleys. Rivers of it. The Withren sat on it and called it theirs. Sitting on a thing doesn't make it yours.
The Magmari carried our war-bands over the lava seas. For pay. Then they wept when it went wrong. They should have charged more.
After every fight the Weft crept in and took bones. Ours and theirs. Their looms still click with our grandsires.
We wore gold so we'd know our own in the smoke. Nobody else would wear it. That's why gold-wearers live here and the rest don't.

lines.text: We were winning. Remember that. Whatever the ash-faces tell you, we were winning.

replies.text: Good. Gold-wearing AND smart. Rare.
Then the Withren cheated. Ask me about the fire some time. Not yet. When I trust you more.
WERE WE? We were winning with our TUSKS! Go away before I show you!

lines.text: The war began over one ingot. A Withren refused to sell us a vein. We took the vein. They took our envoy. We took their valley. You can guess the rest.
We blew the war-horns so long the lava rippled. That's not a story. That's what lava does when you're loud enough.
We marched under banners of red and gold. They came in grey and bone. Their silence scared us more than their blades. So we sang. Loudly. All the way into the valleys.
The Bastions were the war-forts then. Every one a hoard-hold, with a Brute on every tower. We thought we'd never lose one.
The war-chiefs fought over who would lead. By the time they agreed, the Withren had dug in. That's Piglin tactics: shout first, plan later.
Soul sand slowed us. It didn't slow them. You can't win a race when the ground holds your boots.
Some of our dead never came home. The Weft had them first. 'A bone is a bone,' they'd say. A name isn't. Nobody could argue.
The Hold keeps a torn banner from the war, red gone brown, behind the Hoard. We take the whelps to look. We tell them: this is what it costs.
Everyone says Piglins started it. Some say the Withren. I say long ago someone said 'mine' to a hole in the ground, and someone else said 'mine' louder.
I'd end the grudge if I could. Not for the Withren. For the whelps. They shouldn't inherit a fight they can't even spell. Don't tell the Hold. It's a quiet thought.
Would you have fought in it?

replies.text: In a heartbeat! You'd have lasted two. But it was a brave heartbeat.
Run! Hm. Honest. Half the Hold ran. We just don't sing about that part.
The right side. Which is ours. Obviously. Obviously ours.

lines.text: The war taught Hunters patience. Wait for the Withren to blink. They don't blink. We waited anyway. They struck first.
We melted every spare ingot into armour. Every pot, every plate, every earring. The war ate gold faster than a hoglin eats fungus.
My grandmother made war-helmets. Said they were the finest ever. They were also the first melted down, because they dented. Pride goes first.
These halls were a war-hold. See the arrow-slits? The grooves in the floor where the gold carts ran? That's the war, dried into stone.
I've met old soldiers on the road. They don't boast. That's how you know it was bad.
Hoglins went to war too. Herd after herd, charging the valleys. They're why we got as far as we did. A hoglin doesn't know when to stop. We named a clan for that.
After the war the first thing Piglins built was the barter ring. Before roofs. Before walls. Trade first, then rebuild. A Piglin knows his priorities.
I find pale bone blades in the crimson roots sometimes. Old Withren work, cracked. I don't touch them. I mark the spot and leave.
War. Long ago. Brutes were made for it. Now we stand at gates. Not much changed. Hrm.
Grandfather was a Brute in the war. Never spoke of it. I asked once. He said: 'Stand.' That's all. I stand.
Most of the war was waiting. Waiting for orders, waiting for food, waiting for the Magmari to turn up. We were very good at waiting. We shouted about it.
There's a song about the war. One verse is a battle, one is a feast, and all the rest are rude. Shall I sing the first verse? No. The Brutes would cry.
We called it the War of the Hoard because we wanted the Hoard. The Withren called it something else. Ask them. Bring a snack. It'll be a long answer.
We told the whelps we won. Then the Wither came, and we stopped telling it. Now we say: we survived. It sounds smaller. It's bigger.

lines: The Withren made a monster out of three of their own. The Last Answer, they call it. Answer to what? To us. We were the question.
It came over the wastes with three heads screaming. The bastions went up like kindling. Gold ran down the walls like lava.
It didn't stop with us. It burned the Moorings, then the Withren's own forts. They made a thing that ate its makers. Ha. Not funny. A bit funny.

lines.text: You're standing in what it left. The black on these walls isn't paint, and the cracks aren't old age.
Outsiders make Withers now, from Hollowed skulls. Your folk. Would you ever?

replies.text: Good. Then you can stay. Say never again. Good.
Beat it? It doesn't fight, it burns! You don't beat fire. You just lose to it slower.
MAYBE? Out! No. Stay. But I'm watching your hands now.

lines.text: We call it the Burning. Not the Last Answer. That's their pretty word. There was nothing pretty about it.
Ever seen a wall melt? We watched them run. Gold, stone, banner, all one colour at the end. Orange, then black.
My grandsire was on a bridge when the first head came over. He says it didn't look at him. That's what scared him. He wasn't worth looking at.
The horns blew, and then the horns stopped. That's the part the old ones don't say. The horn is the loudest thing we have. When it stopped, everyone knew.
The Brutes held the vault doors while the walls burned. Some doors held. Some Brutes didn't. We name the doors after them.
It wasn't alive and it wasn't dead. Three skulls and a lot of angry soul sand. It wanted something. We never learned what. Maybe it just wanted to stop.
The Hollowed rattle in the old forts. They're Withren it burned out. They carry black swords. If you meet one, run. Don't shout. Run quietly.
Strangest thing: after the Burning, the Withren came to our ashes. They stood there and said the names of our dead too. We nearly fought them. We didn't.
I've never been inside a Fortress. I don't want to. I've seen their towers from the lava's edge, black and empty. They built that. Then they built the thing that made this. Funny how that goes.
My mother was in the east hall when it came. She got out. She never walked through that hall again, not even after the roof was fixed. She walks round. Still.
I'll tell you what I dream. Not the Wither. The quiet after. A whole Bastion and not one voice in it. I wake up and shout something stupid, just to hear a Piglin.
Does it frighten you?

replies.text: Good. Honest fear keeps you alive. I'd worry about a pink-skin who wasn't scared.
NO? Ha! You haven't watched a wall melt. Keep that thought. Lose it slowly.
Now that's the right fear. Not the monster. The ones holding the skulls.

lines.text: The Wither's path is still out there, a line of black stone through the wastes. Nothing grows on it. I cross it sometimes. Like stepping over a scar.
Gold melts at a certain heat. The Wither's fire was hotter. It melted the gold, then the stone, then the vault door. I stand at my furnace and feel small.
We found one gold helm after the Burning, melted onto a wall. We left it. A helmet and a wall, fused. The best piece I've ever seen and the worst.
I never take soul sand in a trade now. Not once. People call it superstition. I call it manners.
There's a shadow on the east wall shaped like a Piglin. A Brute, mid-stride, burned into the stone. We don't scrub it. We say hello when we pass.
I've seen where its heads passed. Nothing's grown since. Not even fungus. The wastes forgive a lot, but not that.
Odd: along the edges of the burn lines the shroomlights come up fat and bright. Something in the ash. I don't ask. I pick. And shiver.
Hoglins still won't graze near the old burn lines. They smell it, I think. Hoglins always know. It's why I trust them more than Piglins.
Wither. Burned. Brutes died. Hrm.
Vault door held. Then it didn't. Brute behind it held. Then he didn't. We carved his name. I check it.
Some say the Three wanted to die. Some say they meant to save everyone. I say dead is dead and burned is burned. But the Three get one nugget from me every year, for the effort.
If it came again, I'd fight it. With a crossbow. And I'd lose. And I'd shout at it all the way down. That's a Piglin's honour: shout and burn.
The Withren say it was a mistake. I say a mistake you make with three skulls and a valley of souls is a decision.
Gold doesn't burn. It melted, yes, but it never burned. We dug it back out of the ash. That's the Piglin answer to the Wither: dig it back out.

lines: Ash-dark skin, Wither faces, and a name for every dead thing. They sat on the gold under the valleys like it was an egg.
The Withren remember every name they ever lost. We remember every bastion they burned. Fair trade.
A Withren never shouts. Never laughs. Never haggles. How do you trust somebody like that? You don't.
They light everything with soul fire. Blue, cold, nasty stuff. We can't stand near it. They know that. They do it on purpose.

lines.text: Ever been to a Vigil? Did they bore you to death?

replies.text: Ha! They tried that on us for a whole war. When boring us didn't work, they made the Wither.
Don't go. Too quiet. A Piglin would go mad from all that quiet.
Kind. Kind is how they get you. Watch your back. Watch your gold.

lines.text: The Withren don't eat. Or if they do, I've never seen it. Nobody's watched one tear into a hoglin leg. I find this deeply suspicious.
I heard they sleep standing up, in rows, like standing stones. I tried standing up to sleep once. I fell on a hoglin.
Their lanterns are blue and their voices are low. Everything about a Withren is a funeral. Even the dinner.
A Withren walked past my camp once. Didn't draw a blade. Didn't shout. Just nodded. I've never been so insulted in my life.
They carve bone into little tokens, a name on each. Piles of them. A pile of names. More treasure than I'll ever have, and I couldn't spend a single one.
Between us? Their wart brew smells good. Hot and bitter. I got a sip once from a thrown pot. I swore to the Hold I spat it out.
Three of them stood at the edge of my Hold once, just standing. We didn't know whether to attack or invite them in. The Brute blew the horn. They left. I'm not proud.
I think we hate each other because we're alike. We both keep what we love. They keep names. We keep gold. They're just quieter about it.
If the war ever truly ended, I'd sit with one of them and hear them say the name of every one of mine. I'd cry. Then I'd deny I cried. Then I'd go home.
A Withren offers you a lantern. Do you take it?

replies.text: Of course? It's blue fire in a jar! ...Fine. Politeness. Just don't bring it into my longhouse.
Never! Yes! A pink-skin who knows better than to take blue fire from a stranger.
Ha! A gold lantern! I'd take it too. I'd take it and run.

lines.text: Withren tracks are odd: no stride, just a smooth drag, as if they glide. A hunter notices these things. A hunter also notices when to run.
Their blue soul fire won't heat my furnace. I've tried. It just makes the gold look sad. Everything it touches looks sad.
They wear bone and basalt, never gold. If they wore gold I'd respect them a little. I might even sell them a ring. At triple the price, of course.
A Withren came to the ring once with a bag of little bone charms. I said I don't take bone. They said it's not for you, and left. Strangest barter I never made.
They come to the edge of the Bastion sometimes. They stand and look at the ash. We don't shoot. We don't wave either. We let them look.
I crossed the Soul Sand Valley twice. Fast. The Hollowed rattle, the sand grabs your boots, the blue light makes you see things. I left a pack behind. It's probably haunted by now.
Nether wart grows in tidy rows on their terraces. Tidy! No Piglin ever grew a tidy row. We pick it wild in the soul sand and complain.
Hoglins hate the Withren's lantern light. They squeal and scatter. So do I, a little. But not as well as a hoglin.
Withren. Quiet. Dangerous quiet. Hrm.
A Withren stood at the gate once. Looked at me. I looked at it. Neither moved. Best watch of my life.
Their children are cute. Don't tell anyone I said that. Big heads, small bodies. Like a Piglin whelp that's learned to be sad.
They call us thieves, you know. I can't prove they're wrong. I can prove they're rude.
A Withren once told me I looked well. Then added: 'Considering.' Considering WHAT?
A Withren says it's sorry about the Wither. Then it says it isn't sorry enough. I can't stand it! Say sorry once and be done!
They have exactly one joke. I've heard it three times. It's about a skeleton and a very long wait. I laughed all three times. It's a good joke. I'd never say so to them.

lines: Lava-walkers. They ferried us to war for pay, and the Wither burned their Moorings for it. Bad bargain. Their own fault.
Gold melts on their skin. Imagine! Can't wear it, can't hold it. No wonder they shiver and grumble so much.
Their striders are fat and slow and full of good meat. We borrow one now and then. They call it raiding. We call it borrowing.
A Magmari never shows gold. So a Magmari is never a friend. Not my rule. Gold's rule.

lines.text: Did a Magmari ever ferry you anywhere?

replies.text: Ha! Did they haggle the whole way? They haggle the whole way. Count your fingers when you land.
Good. Walk on your own feet, wear your own gold, owe nobody. That's the Piglin way.

lines.text: A Magmari walks into lava like I walk into a feast. No fuss. No boots. A cheerful hello to the heat. It's unnatural. I've tried. I have the scars.
Their crests are basalt columns with little vents. They steam when they're angry. Watch for the steam. If you see steam, apologise fast.
They trade in chain. Everything's chain. Chain for fish, chain for fungus, chain for friendship. A people so fond of metal, and not one of them can hold gold.
I saw a barge cross the lava sea once. Magmari singing, striders humming. Beautiful, in a way. I shot at it anyway. Tradition.
When they get far from the lava they cool, go dark and grumpy. I've seen it. A grumpy Magmari is a sad sight. I almost felt sorry. Almost.
Our grandsires paid them in warped fungus, sack after sack. The Magmari love the stuff and we can't stand it. The one fair trade the war ever made.
They eat things roasted in the lava. I had a bite from a plate left at the shore. Sweet first, then smoky, then gone. I ate the whole plate.
The truth is, the Magmari burned for us. Our war-bands rode their barges and the Wither came for the barges. They never said it. They didn't have to. Paid in fungus, burned for it.
When I was young I saw a Magmari child crying over a cold coal. I watched from the hill, with my bow. I put the bow down. Never told anyone. Ever since, I aim a little to the left.
A Magmari wants to trade with you. Will you haggle?

replies.text: Why not? Because they haggle until your ears fall off. Good luck. I mean it. I'd pay to watch.
Sensible. A Magmari trade is a swamp. You go in for a chain and come out owing them a hoglin.
Now that's a Piglin! Name it. Then double it. Then shout.

lines.text: Strider meat is rich, oily and a little sweet. A real feast. The Magmari say a strider is a boat first and supper last. I say supper is supper. That's the whole trouble between us.
They live in heat and I get a headache from my furnace. Lucky creatures. Unlucky skin.
Striders and hoglins don't mix. Striders sulk, hoglins charge. I let one into the pens by accident once. We both learned things.
A Magmari trader came to the border once, hands up, chain-bag open. I'd have bartered until my tongue dried. The Hold said no. I still wonder what was in the bag.
I've heard a golden hoop goes soft and runs if you so much as hand it to a Magmari. I've never tried. I'd hate to see good gold cry.
The Moorings burned the same time as our halls. I think of it when the lava glows in the cracks. Their chain bridges, their hearths. Same black ash as mine.
Cross the lava sea? I'd rather swim in soul sand. A barge costs a fortune and the captain talks the whole way. I've only ever watched them from the shore.
They love warped fungus. We hate it because of the hoglins. They take sackfuls off the Weft. Everyone's stealing from someone. It's a lovely world.
Magmari. Lava. No gold. Hrm.
Watched a Magmari whelp across the lava once. Chasing sparks. Hrm. Looked fun.
Their talk is all hisses and pops. Sounds like a fire arguing with itself. I like it. I'll deny it if you repeat it.
They greet by touching crest-tips. Imagine! A head-butt, only polite. I'd be so confused I'd hit someone.
They won't eat until the hearth is lit. A guest warms first, then eats. A good custom. I could use a hearth before my stew.
Their chains hold a Mooring together. Break one and a bridge falls. Everyone's a link. The most un-Piglin idea I ever heard. Piglins are loose coins in the same purse.
Steam on the lava sea, from far off, looks like a thousand cooking pots. Whenever I see it I get hungry and homesick at once. Don't ask me why.

lines: Four arms, six eyes, and not one honest bone. Well. Plenty of bones. Ours. They took them after the war.
We climb the warped canopy for shroomlights. They drop nets on us. We cut the nets. They make more nets. It goes on and on.
They weave everything into one long cloth. History, they say. I bet we're in it, looking bad.

lines.text: Ever been caught in a Weft net?

replies.text: Lucky. They leave you hanging there and click at you. *click click* Like that. Awful.
Ha! Then you're one of us! We sit round the hearth and complain about it. Loudly.

lines.text: A Weft climbs a stem faster than I fall off one. Four arms! FOUR! I have trouble with two.
They click their jaws when they think. *click click* It's the most annoying noise in the Nether. I hear it in my sleep. Always followed by a net.
From far off a Loom glows like a lit hearth. A thief's eye sees a hearth and thinks: easy. A thief's boot finds out otherwise.
A Weft net isn't a net. It's a lesson. It teaches you not to reach for what isn't yours. I've learned it three times. I'm a slow student.
The Weft sit very still and watch. A Piglin can't stand being watched without a fight. They've won every staring match we've ever had.
They spin thread from a fat caterpillar. A silkgrub! Round, glowy, cute. I nearly took one home. Then I remembered the nets. Cute things come with nets.
I met a Weft outside the forest once. Alone. Lost. It clicked at me, I yelled at it, we both walked away. Best conversation I ever had with a four-arm.
They weave everything they see. Stand still long enough and they'd weave you in. I saw a cloth with a Piglin on it, looking embarrassed. Might have been me.
I once saw a Weft hold a Piglin's shed tusk very gently, turning it over like it mattered. I don't know why. It stayed with me.
If the Weft ever wove me into the Long Cloth, I'd want one row to say we were wrong about the shroomlights, and they were wrong about the bones. Both, side by side.
Do you think the Weft are brave?

replies.text: Brave! Hm. They drop out of a tree onto a Piglin with a crossbow. Fine. Brave. Stupid-brave. But brave.
Sneaky! YES! Thank you! I've been saying it for years and nobody listens.
Careful. That's the word. Careful as a hoglin on a rope bridge. Annoying. Effective.

lines.text: I got netted outside a Loom, hung by one foot, shroomlight in hand. A Weft child walked by, looked at me, looked at the light, looked at me. Then cut me down and took the shroomlight.
Weft hide in the canopy like fruit. You think it's a shroomlight? Blink. It's an eye. Learn the difference or lose a finger.
The Weft use hot dyes. I use hot gold. We'd get on. I'd like to trade tips. Then they'd net me. So no.
Their needles are bone and beautiful. I'd pay for a set. Then I remember where the bone comes from. Then I wish I could pay anyway. Shame on me.
A Weft trader came near our ring once with a cloth. Silky, glowing teal. I'd have bartered gold for it. The Hold said no. That cloth haunts me. In a good way.
Never take a hoglin into the warped forest. It will charge a Weft and the Weft will charge back. Four arms against four legs. I won't say who wins.
We hang cloth in the Bastion to keep the draft out. Weft-made, traded through hands I can't name. Thanks to whoever.
I slept under a Weft bridge once. Safe from the Rotted, safe from the wind. When I woke there was a cup of something warm on a ledge. I never saw who left it. I drank it. It was good.
Weft. Four arms. Annoying. Hrm.
Weft net on my axe once. Took an hour to cut. Hrm. Respect.
The Weft raise their young in the canopy. Little ones, two arms, huge eyes. I saw one drop from a branch and catch itself. Something happened in my chest. Pride? For them? Weird.
They hear it when a warped stem is cut. All the way across the forest. Every Weft in the Loom stops and turns toward you. Never cut a stem. The net taught me.
I admire their patience. I haven't got any. If I'd woven the Cloth, one row a year, it would be finished. Badly. With a lot of shouting. But finished.

lines: Pale, floaty, always crying. From below they look like ghast whelps, so the crossbows go up. Mostly they were whelps. Mostly.
They cry for everybody. Even for Piglins, I heard. Waste of tears. Nobody should cry for a Piglin. They should cheer.
The ghasts that shriek at our walls were Ghastkin once, they say. Then they should come and collect them.
A Ghastkin never wears gold. A pity. Gold would cheer them right up.

lines.text: I shot at one by mistake once. Heard it cry. Real crying, not a ghast shriek. I put the crossbow down. It floated off still crying, and I'm still not sure who I made sad.
They drift without feet. Imagine! A whole people with no feet. How do they kick anything?
They say one good cry washes a bad time away. I tried it once. Cried for ages. Felt worse. Then I hit a wall and felt better. That's the Piglin way.
Their tears heal, they say. One drop. I'd pay an ingot for a vial. But you can't buy a Ghastkin's tear. They have to want to give it. What kind of trade is that?
If you meet a Ghastkin, drop your crossbow first. Then your voice. Then maybe your gold. They flee from loud noises. I find that hard.
Their whelps have open eyes, did you know? They can't cry yet. They look at you like you're the whole world. I've never felt so big, or so small, in one look.
They sing in the Deltas sometimes. Very low, very long. From the ridge it sounds like a hoglin giving birth to a bell. It's pretty. I stay and listen.
The ghasts are the saddest sight in the Nether. A shriek is a cry nobody answers. If the Ghastkin could bring them home, they would. We'd keep shooting, I think. But I'd feel worse.
I lost a brother once. I never cried; Piglins don't. I'd like to try, once, with a Ghastkin beside me, to see what they see. Then I'd hit a wall. But I'd like to try.
A Ghastkin offers to cry for you. Allow it?

replies.text: YES? You'd sit there and let a stranger cry for you? That's braver than a Brute at a gate.
Sensible. Keep your own tears. They're yours. Keep them wherever you keep your gold.
If it helps. Hm. That's a Ghastkin answer. You're half one already.

lines.text: Ghast hunting is half sport, half fear. The Ghastkin look like whelps but cry in whispers. Once you've heard the whisper you know. I hang the crossbow up after that.
I walked the Deltas alone and met a Ghastkin crying over a pebble. I asked what was wrong. It said: it was alive once. I walked on. I'm still thinking about that pebble.
Ghastkin ash-silk doesn't burn, I heard. I'd love a smelter's apron of it. I'd never ask. I'd have to give them something, and I don't know what they want.
Their tear vials are lovely: thin glass, a collar of wire. I'd make a better collar, in gold, with a little hook. They'd never wear it. But I'd still make it.
I tried to barter with a Ghastkin once. It looked at my ingot, looked at me, and gave me a tear for nothing. I felt like a thief, then a fool, then a thief again.
Hoglins don't mind the Ghastkin. They sniff the drifting threads and go back to chewing. I've never seen a hoglin afraid of a Ghastkin, or a ghast, or anything but me with a ladle.
The ghasts circle the Bastion sometimes. Some of them were Ghastkin. I think they know the shape of the place. Maybe they come to mourn. I hate that thought. I think it often.
The Basalt Deltas have the best quartz and the worst footing. I slipped three times. Each time a pale thing floated down, looked at me and floated off. Laughing? Crying? Same face.
Ghastkin. Pale. Quiet. No threat. Hrm.
Small one cried at my gate once. Don't know why. Gave it a nugget. It left. Hope that helped.
They never fight. Not once. How do you win an argument without a fist? They do it by being sad at you. It's very effective.
A Ghastkin once told me my gold was heavy. I said I know, that's the point. It said: not the weight. The wanting. I've been thinking about that for ages.
They hang their homes from cliffs like lanterns. A Piglin would never. Too high, too light, too little room to shout.
The Weft string nets in the air for them. That's rude. I hate the Weft for lots of things, but that one even I find mean.
Once a ghast shrieked at my wall and a Ghastkin drifted up and sang to it. The ghast stopped. Just stopped. Then both floated off together. I put my crossbow away for a good while.

lines: Hoglins: tusks, temper, and the best meat in the Nether. Like a Piglin, but less charming.
Wild ones we hunt. Penned ones we keep. Don't mix them up. The herder will bite you, not the hoglin.
Never bring warped fungus near the pens. Hoglins hate it. The herder hates you for it more.

lines.text: My hoglins? Beautiful. Every one. Even the one that ate my boot. Especially that one. Good taste.
Ever fought a hoglin?

replies.text: Ha! A hoglin-fighter! You're tougher than you look. You look soft.
Do it once. Then never again. That's how everyone learns.
JUST PIGS? Say that in the pens. Go on. I'll watch from up here.

lines.text: A hoglin's tusks never stop growing. File them and they grow back angrier. Don't file them. Let them be. That's the whole secret of keeping a herd.
Baby hoglins squeal like war-horns. A whole pen of them sounds like a band on the march. Sweet. Terrible. Sweet.
Crackling wants a flat stone, a hot fire and nobody talking. Talk and it goes chewy. Piglins hate silence and love crackling. It's the great test of the Hold.
Hoglins wallow in warm ash after a meal. A pen with no ash pit is a pen of grumpy hoglins. Like a Hold with no barter ring.
A hoglin charge is three parts temper and one part hope. If you stand still, they swerve. Probably. I wouldn't bet gold on it.
Every herd has a boar who thinks he runs the Hold. He's wrong, but you let him think it. Same as most chiefs.
Hoglin leather for boots. Hoglin hide for drums. Hoglin hocks for stew. The only part nobody can use is the temper. We've tried.
A trick for a charging boar: sing. Any song. The worse, the better. I sing the clan hymn off-key and they back right off. Maybe it's the song. Maybe it's the pain.
I named a hoglin after you. The big one with the scar. Don't be flattered. It bites me too. We're friends.
Most Piglins say hoglins are food. But I've sat in a pen and felt a boar rest its chin on my knee. A beast that could gore me chose to sleep there. That's the deepest trust I know.
Here's my secret: I can't eat the one I raised. Never could. I trade it for another herder's. You eat the hoglin you didn't name. That's the law of the pens.
Would you ride a hoglin?

replies.text: OF COURSE! Hold the tusks. Never the ears. Ears are for the hoglin.
Sensible! They throw you. Then they sit on you. Then they eat your lunch.
A SADDLE! Ha! No. There's a rope and a loud voice. Mostly the rope.

lines.text: Never turn your back on a boar in a good mood. A mood changes faster than a hoglin turns.
I feed them crimson fungus by hand. The first time a young boar took it gently, I cried. I told everyone it was smoke.
My dream is a herd that doesn't flinch when I sneeze. I'll have it before I die. Or I'll die trying.
Wild boars run in bachelor packs. Never in families. They fight over everything, which is a fine lesson for a Hunter. I learned a lot from them.
Hoglins forage too. We fight over the crimson fungus. They win by eating the lot. I win by shouting about it afterwards.
Hoglin fat burns hot and slow, the best thing for a furnace. The herder sells it to me by the barrel and says I'm stealing.
I carve hoglin tusk into rings. A nugget set in a curve of ivory. Looks like nothing. Costs like everything.
Hoglin hide trades for an ingot at the ring, if you're lucky. A tusk for half. A live one? No. We don't barter live ones. They come back and bite the ring.
There were hoglins in the Bastion once, in the east stables. After the fire the herd went wild. Their young still come to the stable doors. They stand there. We feed them. They never come in.
Wild herds move, and I follow. Not close. You don't share a fire with a herd you mean to hunt. That's rude and also fatal.
Hoglin. Good meat. Hrm. Brute likes hoglin. Hoglin does not like Brute.
When a hoglin is angry its bristles stand up and it huffs. You can smell the rage. Hot rock and old fungus. Like a Piglin after a long argument.
Warped fungus turns a hoglin around in mid-charge. I saw a boar skid ten paces on its haunches. It looked so insulted. I'm still laughing.
They say if a hoglin comes to your door, the clan is blessed. If it comes in and eats your boots, the clan is blessed and poor.
A herd has a pecking order nobody explains and everybody knows. It's the same order as a Hold's. Tells you where we learned it.
Hoglins go Rotted too, if they wander through a portal. A Rotted hoglin attacks anyone, even other hoglins. Sad business. Keep a fungus pot close.

lines: Gold blocks. Chests. Things older than the fire. And a Brute who'd eat you before you got halfway to any of it.

lines.text: Every Piglin in the Hold puts in. Every Piglin can count it. We count it a lot. It's the best game there is.

lines: The Hoard isn't for spending. It's for having. Having is the whole point. Your folk never understand having.
Take from the Hoard and every Piglin near comes for you, gold or no gold. That's the oldest law there is.

lines.text: The vaults below still hold the old Hoards. The fire couldn't eat the gold. It only melted it into new shapes.
Want to see the Hoard some time?

replies.text: Admire. From the gate. With your hands where the Brute can see them. Good answer.

replies.ask: I'd love a bit of it.
replies.text: THIEF TALK! I'll pretend I didn't hear that. Once.

lines.text: The Hoard keeps a tally of who put in what. Every nugget has a name scratched on it. Mine is on thirty. Small ones. But thirty.
To add to the Hoard you stand before the Brute, put a hand on the gold block, and say your name and what you give. The Brute says 'hrm'. That's the receipt.
The Hoard is the only place in the Hold where nobody shouts. Even the loud ones go quiet. It's like walking into a very expensive nap.
Some chests in the Hoard are older than the fire. They haven't been opened in generations. We know what's in them. Nobody wants to be the one who says it aloud.
The Hoard pays for the feasts, the walls and the horn's new rope. Without it we're a gang of shouting hoglins. With it we're a Hold.
A Hoard-thief gets a notch cut in the left tusk. Everyone knows. Nobody forgets. You can't barter with a notched tusk. You can't even stand in line.
When the numbers disagree, we recount. When they disagree again, we recount louder. In the end the Brute grunts an answer. Nobody argues with the grunt.
A Hoard has a heartbeat, they say. The gold ticks as it cools. Put your ear to a block and listen. *tink... tink* Sounds like a very slow hoglin.
I'd put you in the Hoard if I could. A friend's worth more than a block. But you'd complain about the shelf.
The elders keep the Hoard's key. A real key, gold, of course. It's passed on at the greatest feast. I held it once, for a breath. It weighed more than my first tusk.
If the Hold ever had to choose, the Hoard or you, I'd ask them to count again. And again. Until the numbers changed. That's the Piglin way of saying: you. Always you.
Tell me true: would you ever steal from it?

replies.text: Never! Good! The Brute heard that. He's nodding. He doesn't nod. Whatever you said, keep saying it.
A rival's Hoard. Hm. That's ambition, not theft. ...It's theft. But I like the ambition.
EVERYBODY? Name one. ...Me? Not me. Not lately. Get out of my face.

lines.text: Some vault doors still stand shut, the locks melted into the frame. We think the gold's still inside. We knock on them sometimes. Nothing knocks back. Never the black door in the lowest hall, though.
On the way to the vault you pass the Treasure Hall: golden chairs fused to the floor, banners turned to ash, one golden sword stuck in the stone. Nobody pulls it. It's a rule. Don't ask.
The Hoard sits in the middle of the longhouses so everyone's close and nobody can sneak. Piglin design. We hate being watched and love being watchers.
Hoard. Quiet place. Good place. Brute likes quiet.
Sometimes I put my hand on the gold block. Just rest it. It's warm. Nobody sees. Hrm.
Part of the Hoard is my best work, set aside for when the Hold is rich enough to wear it. It's rich enough. The elders keep saying not yet. I keep saying now.
Every ingot in the Hoard passed through my furnace or a friend's. I can tell mine by the surface: a little rough, like a hoglin's chin. Rough means honest.
A good Hoard is built on small trades. A nugget from a barter, an ingot from a hunt, a block from a victory. The ring feeds the Hoard. I feed the ring. Most important chain in the Hold.
Every Hunter puts a tusk from their first kill in the Hoard. Mine's in there. Third shelf, left. It's tiny. Still there. That's all that matters.
Foragers bring shroomlight and quartz to the Hoard. They glow in the vault like little hearths. The Brutes pretend not to look.
My herd has paid into the Hoard more than I have. Their hides, their tusks, their sacrifice. I'd put a hoglin on the tally if it could count.
Wanderers don't have a Hoard. We have a pouch. Every Wanderer dreams of a vault. Every Wanderer fears one too. Funny how that goes.
My cousin got caught with a nugget in his boot at the Hoard gate. The Brute held him by the ankle, upside down, till it fell out. We all watched. We all laughed. Then we all checked our own boots.
Things in the Hoard that aren't gold: a fossil tusk, a Weft needle, a bone token from a Withren. Spoils of old wars. Kept so we remember what each one cost.
First rule of the Hoard: don't. Second rule: really, don't. Third rule: the Brute.
Brutes are the biggest and the meanest. They don't barter, they don't laugh. They carry axes and they stand there.
Every Hold keeps two Brutes. One at the Hoard, one on the horn. Both of them are glaring at you. Right now.
Brutes respect gold. Except in a bastion vault. Down there, gold is just what they take off your body.
Want a secret? Brutes are born small, like the rest of us. They just never stop being angry about it.
Me. Big. Axe. Done.
Brute doesn't talk much. Talk is for traders. Brute is for gates.
You. Strong?

replies.text: Hrm. Good.
Hrm. No. Brave, though. Brave is good.
Hrm. Then stay behind me.

lines.text: A Brute chooses the gate. Or the gate chooses the Brute. Either way, nobody leaves it.
Brutes eat first and last. First because they're hungry. Last because they were guarding. Nobody argues.
If a Brute likes you, he'll stand next to you. Not talk. Just stand. That's the highest praise there is. I stood next to one once. For a long, long while.
Their axes are gilded at the edge. If one breaks, the Hold melts a helmet to replace it. So don't break it.
A Brute doesn't haggle, laugh or lose. All three together make him the ideal guard and the worst guest at a feast.
The Hold calls its two Brutes Gate and Horn, after their posts. They have real names. Nobody uses them. Except the whelps.
Young Brutes train by hitting the same log until it stops being a log. Then the next one. The Hold has no logs left.
Brutes sleep like hoglins by a fire: half an eye open, half a nose out. I dropped a nugget in the vault once and found an axe at my throat.
They say Brutes dream. Of what, nobody knows. I asked one. He said: 'Gate.' I asked again. He said: 'Open gate.' That's the closest to a poem I ever heard from one.
A Brute stands before a mountain of gold and wants nothing. I think that's the heart of it. The strongest of us is the one who doesn't reach.
Would you challenge a Brute?

replies.text: Wise. A challenge to a Brute is a very short story.
A fair fight with a Brute. Ha! Ha. ...Have you got a will? Leave me your gold.
FRIENDS! Cleverest thing I've heard in ages. He'd still win.

lines.text: A Brute can track a thief by smell. Across lava, through the forge, round three corners. I've seen one find a nugget in a barrel of ash. They'd make fine hunters. They won't leave the gate.
Brutes make me nervous at the furnace. They stare at the molten gold like it's alive. Then they nod. I don't know what they're agreeing to.
The Brute's axe is my hardest commission. They want it light and heavy at once. I say that's impossible. They look at me. I make it.
Brutes never barter. But sometimes one stands behind my ring when a deal goes sour. He says nothing. The deal fixes itself. Brilliant.
Hoglins respect a Brute. A boar backs off from an axe-glint. I borrow one for the worst herding. They glare at each other until it's over.
I once watched a Brute eat a fungus. Just stood there chewing. Never moved a muscle. When he was done he said: 'Hrm.' Nicest thing anyone's said about a fungus.
The Brutes in our Bastion never left their posts after the fire. Some still watch an empty hall. We bring them food. They eat. They stare. They hold.
Brutes are why I don't rob Holds. Not honour. A Brute is a wall with a grudge.
Brute stands. Stands is good.
Brute likes quiet. Brute likes gold. Brute likes you. Little. Hrm.
When I was small, someone laughed at me. Now no one laughs. That is why Brute. Hrm.
Brute has a hoglin. At home. Named it Small. It is not small. Hrm. Funny.
Tusk-kin. If gate falls, Brute falls first. If you are in trouble, Brute walks. Leaves the gate. Only for you.
They don't wear much. The scars are the real armour.
Nothing so funny as a bribe delivered to a Brute's face. He holds it a while, then gives it back. With interest. A broken nose, usually.
If a Brute walks toward you with his axe lowered, you're fine. If he walks toward you with it raised, you were fine. Now you're not.
Brutes in a Bastion vault aren't cruel. They're loyal to a room. The room is gold. Half the gold is gone. They guard the walls anyway. That's loyalty no ingot can buy.
They say a Brute runs only once. Then he never leaves a gate again. The old story: a Brute left his post, and the Hold fell. So they stand till they fall.

lines: A Brute! No, a Bartermaster! No, a Brute who barters! Nobody would ever say no to me.
I'm going to have the biggest gold pile in the whole Hold. Bigger than the Hoard. Bigger than {neighbour}'s.
When my tusks come in I'm going to bite a hoglin back. The one that bit me. I know which one.

lines.text: Will you help me get rich? Please? Lots?

replies.text: YES! You're the best gold-wearer ever! I'm telling everyone!
Work? That's what grown-ups say. Boring grown-ups. Are you a boring grown-up?

lines.text: I want to blow the war-horn! Just once! I'll blow it so loud the lava jumps!
I'm going to be a Goldsmith and make a helmet for a hoglin. A tiny gold helmet. Nobody ever thought of it.
I want to be a Wanderer! Go everywhere, shout at everyone, come home with a pocket full of news. And nuggets. Mostly nuggets.
Maybe a Smelter. They get to burn their eyebrows off and nobody tells them no. Imagine that!
I'll be the biggest, loudest, shiniest Piglin ever. Taller than the horn tower! Then I'll sit on the Hoard. Is that a job?
When I'm big I'll have a hoglin and we'll go everywhere together. His name's Bitey. No, that's taken. Bitey Three!
I wished for a pet hoglin. I got a baby hoglin. It ate my shoe. I gave it the other one.
I want to be a Brute but I'm scared of the Brute's face. When I'm a Brute will I be scared of my own face? Is that how it works?
I want to be like you! Shiny and brave. Do you give lessons? I can pay in nuggets. I have one nugget. Two pebbles.
When I grow up I'll let you into the Hoard whenever you like. I'll be the Brute at the gate. I'll say 'Hrm.' Then I'll let you in. Deal?
I'm only telling you. I don't want to be loud. I want to be kind. If the others find out I'll deny it. Loudly.
When I grow up I'll find a way for you to live in the Hold. A real house, with a hearth and everything. I'll tell the elders. I'll yell until they listen.
What do you think I should be?

replies.text: A Hunter! Yes! Crossbow, big boots, lots of shouting! I'll start practising on a nugget. A nugget doesn't bite back.
A Goldsmith! I'd make you a helmet. A GOLD helmet! With a horn on it! Is a horn a good idea?
A BRUTE! You think I could? You think I could! I'm telling everyone! I'm telling the Brute!

lines.text: My mother says I can be anything if I shout loud enough. I'm practising. AAAAAA! See? Anything!
I want to be somebody they write over the gate. In gold paint. With a picture of my face and lots of tusk.
I'll be a Bartermaster and give everyone gravel. Everyone! And they'll love it! Because gravel is funny!
I want to jump the lava. All the way across. The grown-ups say don't. That means it's possible.
When I'm big I'll have a very very deep voice and say 'hrm'. Hrm. Hrm. How did I do?
Maybe a Forager. I'll find a shroomlight bigger than my head. The Weft will drop nets and I'll be too fast. Whoosh!
I want to be the one who counts the Hoard. All of it! One by one! Then start again. It never ends! Best job!
When I'm big I'll rebuild the east hall with my own hands. The Brutes will help. The hoglins will help. And the gold will be everywhere, like before.

lines: Hoglin riding! You climb on a little one and hold on. It bites. You win if you don't cry.
Snatch! You grab some gold and run. Grown-ups chase you. Best game in the Nether.
Horn! One of us is the horn and shouts, and everybody jumps on {neighbour}. They don't like this game.

lines.text: Secret: {neighbour} cried when their baby hoglin ran off. Big crying. Don't tell. I didn't tell you.
Tusk-tug! Two of us hold a stick in our teeth and pull. Whoever lets go loses. I've never lost. I've also never won. We're still pulling.
Ash-hop! Hop from stone to stone and the ash is the lava. Real lava is for grown-ups. Falling in ash makes you sneeze. Sneezing loses.
Count-the-Hoard! One of us is the Brute and counts. The rest sneak up and touch the gold block. If you get caught, you're the Brute. Nobody stays caught.
Barter! I'm the Bartermaster. You give me a pebble, I give you a different pebble. They're all pebbles. Everyone loses. It's the best.
Shout-off! Whoever shouts longest wins. A ghast joined in once. She won. We don't talk about it.
Rotted tag! One's the Rotted and shuffles. If he tags you, you shuffle too. It's very funny. And a bit scary. The scary part is why it's funny.
Nugget-hunt! Someone hides a nugget and the rest hunt. It's always in the same place. Nobody learns. I always check under the same stone.
Boot-throw! Who can throw a boot over the pen wall. The record's mine. I hit a hoglin. It was an accident. A glorious accident.
Bridge! Two of us on a plank over the ash. First to wobble is the Rotted. I'm always the Rotted. I wobble on purpose. It's a better part.
Come play! I'll be the hoglin and you be the Hunter. You chase, I charge. When you catch me you get a nugget. That's the rule. I made it.
Hide-in-the-ring! We hide in the barter ring while the Bartermaster's back is turned. When he finds us we sell him a pebble. Best game ever.
My favourite game is the one where you tell me about the Overworld and I guess what's rotten. Clouds? Rotten? Trees? Rotten? You say no and I'm amazed every time.
I made up a new game. It's called Friend. You hide, I find you, and then we both shout. That's all. I only play it with you.
Can I play too?

replies.text: Easy. Shout. If you get caught, shout. If you win, shout twice. That's all of them!
Aww. Fine. FINE! But later? Later you'll play? Say later!
YES! A grown-up hoglin! Charge me! No, wait, I'm the Hunter! I'll chase YOU! Go go GO!

lines.text: The grown-ups don't like Snatch because somebody always gets hurt. We play behind the pens. They find out anyway. By the bruises.
In Horn you have to be the loudest. I'm the loudest! I'm so loud the others stopped playing. So now I play alone. That's still winning, right?
I invented Ghast! You float on your tiptoes and cry out loud. Whoever cries longest wins. Nobody else wants to play.
Gold-block-stack! Build the tallest tower from whatever we find. When it falls everybody screams. Then we build again.
I'm the best at Statue. Stand still. Don't move. Not even to scratch. The Brutes taught me. I've been a statue for ages.
Ash-pies! We make them out of ash. They're not for eating. Well. Not for eating much.
We play Hollowed! You rattle your teeth and walk stiff. I rattle the best. The grown-ups tell us to stop. We rattle quieter.
Rope-tug at the horn tower! You get one tug and run. If the horn goes off, the Brute chases you. It went off once. Nobody's allowed to talk about it.
Hoglin-ring! One of us is the hoglin and everyone else holds hands and keeps it in. It always escapes. It always bites someone. That's how you know it's a good hoglin.

lines: Not scared of anything! Except the blue fire. And the Rotted. And the Brute on the horn when he sneezes.
Grown-ups say if you go through a portal you come back Rotted. I'm never going. Unless there's gold. Then maybe.
Ghasts! They cry so loud. I hide under the bench. Not scared. Just hiding bravely.

lines.text: Secret: Brutes are scared of the blue fire too. I saw one jump. I didn't laugh. Out loud.
Soul sand. It grabs your boot and holds on. I'm not scared. I'm careful. Carefully scared.
The quiet. When the horn stops and nobody talks. It's like holding your breath. I hate it. I shout something. Anything.
Withren! They're tall and grey and they look at you like you've already done something. I haven't! Yet!
The dark room behind the forge. Grown-ups say there's nothing in it. Then why is it so dark?
Falling in lava. Falling in lava. FALLING IN LAVA. There. Done. I said it three times so it won't happen.
Sometimes I dream the Hoard is empty. I wake up and run to check. It's never empty. I check twice.
I'm scared of being small forever. What if my tusks never come in? Grown-ups say they will. Grown-ups say a lot of things.
Weft nets! They come out of nowhere and go zip! and you're hanging. I've been practising falling safely. I'm very good at falling.
I'm scared of the Wither, but only a little, because it's gone. Mostly it's gone. Is it gone?
A big hoglin with a big tusk! Not scared. Interested. From far away. From behind the Brute.
I tell the grown-ups I'm not scared of anything. It's a lie. But if I say it loud enough the scary things think twice. Mostly.
Can I tell you something? When the horn blows I'm scared. Everyone runs toward it and I want to run away. But I run toward it anyway. Because everyone does.
I'm scared you won't come back. Wanderers leave. Hunters sometimes leave and don't come back. You're not allowed. It's a rule. I made it up.
I'm not scared when you're here. Nothing is. Not even the Wither. I'd hide behind you. To me you're taller than a Brute.
Will you stay with me till I'm brave?

replies.text: Promise? Promise promise? Then I'm braver already. A bit. A tiny bit. Don't tell.
Am I? ...I AM! I'm brave! I'm telling the Brute! Brute! BRUTE!
That's what the grown-ups say. They also say eat your fungus. Time is boring.

lines.text: The Rotted at the edge of the Hold. Whenever I look, they're closer. I check every time. They're never closer. That's worse.
Magmari! Everyone says they're nice but they're lava people! How can lava people be nice? Lava isn't nice!
When a Brute smiles. It looks like he's about to eat me. Maybe it's just a smile. Maybe it's both.
The big gold mirror at the goldsmith's. It shows a Piglin who looks like me. But he doesn't blink when I do. He blinks later.
I'm scared of the grown-ups when they're quiet. They're never quiet. When they are, something's wrong.
A ghast came right up to our wall. I held my breath the whole time. Then I breathed and she was gone. I held it again just in case.

lines: I've got a nugget! Two nuggets! One's a pebble I rubbed on the other one. Don't tell.
I found a golden carrot. Well, I found it in {neighbour}'s hand. I ate it. It was hard on the teeth.
My treasure's buried under the hearth. Wait. Forget that. My treasure's somewhere else. Far away.

lines.text: Want to see my treasure? You have to say please.

replies.text: Hmm... NO! Ha! Maybe later. If you give me a nugget. Two nuggets.
THIEF! I'm telling! I'm telling the Brutes!

lines.text: I've got a bone from a hoglin. Tusk-sized. I carved my name on it. {name}. Mostly. The N is backward.
I found a shiny sliver of quartz at the edge of the lava. It's not gold. It's better: it's mine. It goes pink in the glow.
My treasure is a boot. A very good boot. It used to be {neighbour}'s. It's mine now. They don't know. Don't look at them.
A broken gold buckle! A whole one! No, half. It's still shiny. Shiny halves count.
I've got three shroomlights in a bag. I take them out and they glow. It's like having my own little hearth. The Foragers would want half.
I have a Weft needle. Real bone. Sharp! I found it near the forest edge. I'm not supposed to be at the forest edge. Don't tell.
I got a tusk that fell out of a Brute! I was there! It fell right on the ground in front of me! I picked it up and ran. I'm in trouble.
I traded my best pebble for a lump of ash that looks like a hoglin. It's the greatest treasure in the Hold.
A coin from before the fire! It's crooked and has a Piglin's face on it. Maybe a hoglin's. Either way, it's old.
I'll show you my treasure box. It's under the third bench. There's a nugget, a tooth, a bit of rope and a smell. The smell is very important.
I'll share. You can hold the nugget. Just for a bit. Then give it back. If you don't, I'll cry. Loudly. Then the Brutes will come.
My real treasure is a secret. It's not gold. It's a drawing of you. I made it with ash on a stone. It looks like a hoglin in a helmet. But it's you.
You're my treasure. Don't tell. I'd never say that to a grown-up. But you're shiny all the way through. I mean it. You're the shiniest.
Trade you my pebble for your nugget!

replies.text: Ha! A FAIR trade! Grown-ups never say that! Fine! It's a very good pebble. Don't lose it.
Aww. Fine. Maybe when I'm bigger and my pebbles are better.
TWO! You're a genius! A rich genius! Teach me! Teach me everything!

lines.text: I keep a list of everything that's mine. It's very long. It includes the Hoard, the horn and half a hoglin. The elders said no. I said fine, I'm carving it in the bench instead.
Treasure hunting is easy. You walk until you find something shiny. If it's not shiny, you walk further.
I found a hinge in the ash. A gold hinge! Doors have those! Mine is the only hinge in the Hold with no door. I'm going to make a door for it.
My treasure map is a drawing of the Hold with an X. The X is under the horn tower. I haven't dug yet. The Brute's looking.
A golden sword hilt, no blade! Hilt only. So it's safe! A hilt is just a handle! Handles are treasure.
I'm saving my nuggets for something big. I don't know what yet. The elders say save. The Wanderers say spend. I say hide.
I swapped a tooth that fell out for a gold nugget at the barter ring. Nobody checked. I'm rich. I have a tooth-shaped hole.
I collect tusk shavings. Hoglin, Piglin, Brute. Different colours! The Brute ones are yellow.

lines: You hand me an ingot. I hold it up and admire it. Six breaths, no fewer. Then the ring tosses you something. That's the whole trade. The rest is shouting.
Admiring can't be rushed. Gold wants to be looked at. Skip the looking and the ring turns sulky and gives you junk out of spite.
I don't choose what comes out. The gold chooses. I just hold it and take the blame. Hard work, blame. Heavier than an anvil.
No refunds. No swaps. No crying at the ring. A Piglin who cries at a trade has already lost the next one.
Nuggets buy nothing in my ring. Bring an ingot. Bring a block and I'll throw in my stool.
The ring is round so nobody can stand behind it. No corners, no whispering. Whatever you buy, you buy where everyone, {neighbour} included, can see.
The block on the pedestal watches every deal. Cheat, and it knows. How? I don't ask the block. It might answer.
Fire potions, iron boots, obsidian: now we cheer. Crying obsidian, the kind that bleeds purple: now we howl with joy for a count of ten.
Pearls, the green-black ones, roll out of the ring now and then. The whole Hold stops and stares. I charge a nugget for the staring.
You can't barter angry. An angry hand makes an angry ring. Count six, think of roast hoglin, then hold out the gold.
Fools wave the ingot about to get the gold excited. Excited gold gives string. I have sacks of string from fools.

lines.text: Between us? I mutter to each ingot before I admire it. 'Be kind.' Sometimes it is. I'd say one time in four. Which is better than most Piglins manage.
