First kill, they paint your tusks with soot. I strutted about with black tusks trying to look dangerous. I looked like I'd lost a fight with a furnace.
My mother sent me for fungus and I came back with a shroomlight bigger than me. First time they called me a Forager. Last time they sent me alone.
I never had a longhouse as a child. We moved. Every Hold was home for a few Counts and then it wasn't. That's why I'm a Wanderer. Or that's why I say so.
Bastion children play Fire: one is the Wither and runs at the others, shouting. The elders have stopped it twice. It always starts again.
Small. Then big. Then bored.
First gate I guarded, I sat at it and fell asleep. Woke up still guarding. Good.
Mother said, be big. I was.
What were YOU like as a child? Small and shiny?

replies.text: Quiet! Careful! You were a Withren child! A poor sad one.
That's it! That's the stuff! We'd have been friends in the pens.
Ha! A sleeper! Like a hoglin by the furnace. We'd have let you be.

lines.text: The clan is the longhouse. One hearth, one gold block, one big loud tusked mess. One of us is hit, all of us bleed. One of us finds gold, all of us borrow.
Love is a barter where both sides think they won. That's the whole secret. Mine thinks they won. I let them.
Courting is haggling. You offer a ring too small, they refuse it. You offer a ring too big, they refuse it. By the time you get it right, you've spent half your life together.
When two Piglins wed, they weigh each other's gold on the longhouse scale. Equal weight, equal say. Unequal weight, a very loud feast.
A wedding ring never fits at first. That's on purpose. You must go back to the smith to have it sized, and that gives you a reason to talk.
A litter is four, five, six. Mine was five. I was the loudest. Four of us are still alive and still arguing.
My littermates: Gorrak who bites, Mugga who counts, Hurla who runs off, and Ozzik who is Ozzik. I love them all. I'll deny it if you repeat it.
My father taught me everything he knew, which took one long boast. The rest I learned by being hit.
My mother ran our longhouse like a war-camp, with one difference: in a war-camp somebody sometimes wins.
I'm a father of nine! Or seven. One might be {neighbour}'s. We're discussing it.
My daughters are all tusked and furious. I've never been prouder. Show me a mother who isn't proud of a furious daughter and I'll show you a liar.
My sons are hopeless and I love them. One lost his helmet in a lava stream, one sold his boots for a nugget, and one sits near the Hoard looking wise.
A good mate is somebody who hits the same people you hit, and cooks when you can't.
The eldest of a clan is the Old Tusk. Doesn't do anything, doesn't need to. Sits at the hearth, says 'hm,' and the rest of us get nervous.
Clans quarrel over everything: whose hoglins, whose Hoard, whose cousin. Then somebody's hurt and the quarrel vanishes. That's family. It just takes a while to arrive.
When we're apart, my mate and I swap nuggets. Each carries the other's. A pouch with someone else in it is a good thing to carry.
I lost a littermate to a lava ford that looked shallow. I still check every ford twice. Three times if you're watching.
Marrying out of your clan is allowed. Marrying out of your people is... let's say it's an interesting thought. I've had interesting thoughts.
Herder families are the best. We share a roof, a pen and a smell. The smell is family too.
My apprentice is my niece. She's better than me. I tell her so rarely. Never. I told you, so don't repeat it.
A hunter's family waits at the gate with the spit ready. I've never come home empty. The one time I did, they cooked a boot.
According to {neighbour}, I have a family in every Hold. I have one. It's just very spread out.
Families in the Bastion share what's left of one room. Everyone's cousin. Everyone's cousin's cousin. Everyone's snoring.
Family. Hoard. Gate. Same thing.
Had a mother. Big. Louder than me.
Mate? No. Axe. Axe listens.
Have you a mate? A family? Do they know you came down here?

replies.text: Ha! A secret trip! Bring them presents when you tell them. Gold, preferably.
Of course they worry! That's what families do. Mine worry, mine shout, mine borrow my helmet.
Alone! Not here. In a Hold you're somebody's cousin by the next meal.

lines.text: Don't tell {neighbour}. I'm afraid of the blue fire. Not the Withren. The fire. It doesn't flicker like proper fire. It stares.
An empty Hoard. Full, I sleep like a stone. Half, I sleep like a hoglin. Empty... I don't sleep.
The Rotted. Not because they're strong. Because they walk like they remember me.
The Wither coming back. Three heads, no mercy. I dream it. I shout in the dream, which is the only reason I wake.
Quiet. If the Hold goes silent, something is wrong. A loud Hold is a living Hold. A quiet one is a tomb.
A ghast's shriek behind me. Not the shriek. The one after, when it stops and breathes.
Dying with an empty hand. Die with no gold and you die nobody's. That's why we put a nugget in each fist. Check your pouch.
Losing my tusks. Not the pain. The look on people's faces. Tusks are rank. Lose them and the shouting gets smaller.
Getting old and quiet. I'd rather go down in a brawl than shrink in a chair. If I ever sit in a chair, hit me.
Lava seas. Not because I can't swim. Because the Magmari can walk on them and I can't, and they know it.
Debts. Owing is worse than being owed. Owing is a hand on your neck. I'd lose a fight before I'd owe a nugget.
Water. I heard about the Overworld's water. If it touches me, I think I'll hiss.
Portals. Every time I see one I feel a tug in my ankles, like the Overworld wants to take a Piglin home.
Heights. There. I said it. Keep it quiet. Whenever I'm on the horn tower I look at the horn, not the drop.
Being poor and quiet. A poor Piglin can shout and haggle. Poor and quiet is just sitting. Dying slowly.
Being forgotten. The Withren carve names. The Weft weave names. We shout names. Shouts go. Sooner or later my name won't be shouted by anyone.
The silence after a fight, when you count who's missing. That's the worst part of any brawl.
That my young ones will grow up with nothing to boast about. I want them to have stories. Good ones. Even if I have to invent them.
I'm afraid of missing a shot in front of the others. Terror. I practise in secret, behind the pens.
The furnace going out. Not the fire. The silence of a cold furnace. Like a heart that's stopped.
A bad pour. It cracks and shows the weakness, in a ring, in a blade, in a Piglin. Cracks are what I fear.
The pens going quiet. I don't mean sleep-quiet. I mean the other one.
Being at the edge of a Hold when the horn blows and I'm not inside. I have a dream about it. I never reach the gate.
The floor. Half of it is held up by habit. Sooner or later it'll remember it's a ruin. We tell the young not to run in the hall. They run in the hall.
Fear? Blue fire. Sneezing. Quiet. Not much.
Leaving the gate open. Nothing else.
Forgetting the order. Gate. Gold. Hit. Gate. Gold. Hit.
What frightens YOU? Go on. I told you mine.

replies.text: Green boomers! I'd be scared too. Scared and curious. Mostly curious.
Ha! You'll never be alone down here. Somebody always shouts at you. It's a comfort.
NOTHING! Everyone's afraid of something. Fine. Be brave. I'll be loud on your behalf.

topics.ask: How do you honour your dead?

lines.text: We shout the name. As loud as we can, as long as breath lasts, till the roof cracks. A quiet funeral means nobody liked you.
Before the burying, the family weighs the gold the dead one leaves. Not to share it. To say aloud how much they had, so the next of kin can boast on their behalf.
A nugget goes in each fist. That's the ticket. A Piglin walks into the next place with gold in both hands and nobody argues.
We bury outside the Hold, on a rise, in blackstone. Face toward the Hoard, always. So they can still hear us counting.
We plant the dead one's tusks round the grave like a fence. Anyone who wants to rob the grave must get past the tusks. Nobody has.
A Piglin who dies in the Overworld comes back Rotted. So every Piglin has one last task: die at home, even if it means crawling.
Mourning lasts as long as the mourners can go without a joke. That's usually until the second mug of mash.
For those lost in the lava we hold a Loud Wake. We shout their name toward the sea until the ghasts answer. Sometimes they answer. We call that the sea saying yes.
When a ghast shrieks over a grave we leave a nugget on the stone, in case it's somebody's cousin.
We don't weep. We shout, we feast, we hit something. If you must weep, do it in the pens, where the hoglins won't tell.
The Withren keep one dead one each. Odd. We keep them all, in the shouting and the stories and the bad jokes they left behind.
Don't speak ill of the dead, unless it's funny. If it's funny, speak at length. They'd want you to.
Every Remnant keeps a doorpost of soot handprints. Each Piglin who dies in the Bastion gets one, pressed in the old fire's soot. The post is nearly full. We try not to look at it.
The Black Count marks the coming of the fire: we call out the names of the lost, one clap of tusks per name. It takes a long, long while. Nobody leaves.
When my grandsire died we gave him his best helmet, his worst joke and his last debt. He's still owed. We set an empty cup for him at every feast.
A promise made over a grave is the strongest there is. Break it and the whole clan turns on you. I've made one. I'm not telling you which.
When a Piglin dies we pour a small ingot from their ring and stamp it with their clan mark. It goes into the Hoard. Their gold stays.
The hunter's last kill is skinned and the hide laid over the grave. The herd knows to go round it.
When a herder dies, the herd is led past the grave once. Every hoglin sniffs. Some bow. It's very moving. Hoglins are better at this than we are.
We cast their last ingot into a mould shaped like their tusks and everyone gets a piece. I've got three. I don't know whose they are.
A Wanderer's grave is a heap of stones by the road. Passers-by add a stone and a shout. I've added a lot. I'll need a big heap.
Brutes are buried at the gate. Facing out.
Dead Brute's axe goes to the next one. Next one stands.
Name shouted. Once. Loud. Enough.
How does your world honour its dead? Loud, I hope.

replies.text: QUIET?! They'll think nobody cared. Next time bring a horn.
Stories! Yes! Make them big and a little false. The dead don't argue.
Good. Bury them with gold if you have it. You don't? Poor dead.

lines.text: A roof on every longhouse, and not one patch. No, two patches. Patches show we survived.
A Hoard so heavy the floor complains. I'd fall asleep to the creaking.
A litter louder than me. The first one who shouts me down gets half my Hoard.
I hope to see a Bastion made whole again. Every wall, every roof, every hall that used to echo. Not for the gold. For the echo.
I hope the Wither never wakes again, and nobody else gets clever with skulls. I hope your hands stay clean of them.
I hope to find my uncle, the Rotted one. Just to see if there's a Piglin left in there. If there is, I'll bring him home. If not, I'll shout until he remembers.
I want a statue. Gold. Life-sized. With my best helmet and a very flattering nose. Set it in the Hoard.
I hope a Brute smiles. Just once. I'd pay to see it. I'd pay a nugget. A small one.
I hope to live long enough to be the Old Tusk. Sit at the hearth. Say 'hm.' Make everyone nervous.
A peace with the other four? Hm. I'd trade a lot for a quiet road to the next Hold. I wouldn't trade my axe, though.
I hope my song lasts. Just a verse. A rude one. Sung at the Count after I'm gone.
I hope you keep coming back. Every Piglin needs one friend who isn't a Piglin. Someone to impress.
There's a feast in the old tales: gilded crackling on a gold plate, with a gold cup and a gold spoon. They say you can only eat it once. I'll risk it.
I hope the herd doubles. And that the herd's worst-tempered boar learns manners. Not likely.
I hope to forge something that outlasts the Hold: a ring still on a finger when the lava seas run dry.
I hope to drop the biggest hoglin in the Nether with one bolt, from far off, with witnesses. The witnesses are important.
I hope to carry good news. Just once. Every Hold I reach, a horn and a feast because of my news. Mostly it's fires and raids.
I hope the furnace never goes cold. That's all. A warm furnace and a loud roar. What more could a Piglin ask?
I hope the next trip finds a shroomlight bigger than my head, and no Weft watching.
I hope the barter ring never closes. Gold in, goods out, shouting all the way.
I hope we get the east wing back. The fire took it, the sky took the roof, the hoglins took the floor. Lay one stone and I'll lay the second.
Hope? Gate holds. Gold stays. Quiet.
Hope for a nap. Standing. Eyes open.
Hope for young Brutes. Good ones. Better than me. Not by much.
And you? What do you hope for? Gold, I'd guess.

replies.text: FRIENDS LIKE ME! There's only one of me, but I'll be loud enough for several.
Home. Yes. Safe is good. Safe is gold you don't have to count.
Of course. Of course gold. I like you more every time you shine.

loved: GOLD! For me? Hold still, I need to look at it. *snort* Look at it! Everyone, look at it!
Ooh. Ohhh. Right now you're my favourite. Maybe forever. Let's say forever.
Now THAT is a handshake. You and I are going to get along.
I'll put it with my best things. Right next to my other best things. It'll be the best of them.

loved.text: Hrm. Gold. Good.
For ME? Mine! Nobody touch it! *snort* It's the shiniest thing I've got!
Gold! Real gold! Hold it up to the lava-light so I can see it sing. *click* Perfect.
You gave me gold and you didn't even haggle. Are you ill? Are you a fool? Are you after something? I don't care. THANK YOU!
Oh, it's heavy. It's HEAVY. A heavy gift is an honest gift. I'll remember this when I'm counting.
Mine. Mine mine mine. Sorry. Thank you. Mine.
I'll hide it where only I can find it, then forget where, then weep, then find it again. That's love.
You know what I like best about gold? It never says thank you back. I will, though. THANK YOU. Loudly.
Is there a bigger piece? I'm not complaining. I'm asking. Politely. With my tusks.
That's the best thing anyone's put in my hand since... since... Fine, since ever. My mother mustn't hear this.
Look at it shine! It's winking at me! Everyone, it's winking!
This goes in the clan's Hoard. No. In MY Hoard. No. On my body, right now, where it can be seen.
Gold-friend! Gold-FRIEND! I'd carry you on my shoulders if you weren't so heavy with the stuff.
You give me gold and ask for nothing. That's either generosity or a plan. Either way, I'm in.
You didn't have to. That's why it counts. Now sit. I'll find you something nearly as good. Nothing is as good.
From you I'd take gold asleep, in a fight, at my own funeral. Don't ever stop.
Lovely weight. Lovely colour. Stand back, I'm going to examine it with my teeth.
Don't tell me it's raw. Ha! I'd smelt it anyway. It'd look so good as an ingot.
I should give you something back. I'm thinking of something. Still thinking. Thinking very hard.
Good gold makes for a straight shot. I'll carry it where I can feel it.
My hoglins will want a taste. They can't have it. They can look. LOOK, you big idiots. Look, don't bite.
Gold on the road is a friend who doesn't talk back. I'll carry it everywhere. And I'll miss it every time I spend it.
Gold INTO the Bastion! Do you know how long it's been since anyone brought gold in? Every other visitor takes it out.
Gold. Mine. Thank.
Heavy. Good. Brute stays near you now.
Gold gold gold GOLD! For ME? I'll never let go of it!
It's almost bigger than my head! Can I sleep on it? Can I? *snort snort*

liked: Good. Not gold, but good. I'll eat it, or wear it, or bite it. One of those.
Ha! You know what a Piglin likes. Not as well as gold, but close.
That'll do nicely. Hand it over. No, I'll take it. There.
Useful! I approve. I'd approve more if it shone.

liked.text: Hrm. Good.
For me? Thank you! Is it gold next time?
Not gold, but I'll take it. A Piglin never refuses a gift. Only a fool refuses a gift. Or a Withren. Same thing.
Useful! I'll find a place for it. A good place. Second-best, after gold.
Ha, you know your Piglin. A gift that fills a belly or a quiver is worth a handshake.
That'll do nicely. Better than nicely. Nicely and a half.
Thank you. I mean it. I'm not saying it loudly, so you know I mean it.
You've good taste! A little greedy. A little late. But good.
Mm. This I can use, or trade, or boast about. Any of the three is a win.
If I had spare nuggets I'd match it. I've no spare nuggets. So, I'll shout my thanks.
That's two good turns you've done me. Three, if you count not hitting me. Let's count it.
I'd give you a better answer, but I'm busy being moved. Look away. No, don't look.
Good for the trail. I'll use it and tell everyone I found it. Technically I did. In my pack.
I'd have found it myself. In a while. Thanks for saving me the walk.
Keep it away from the furnace. Thank you. Now keep it away from the furnace.
I can do something with this. A fitting for a helmet, a strap for a belt, something with shine on top.
The hoglins will want to eat it. I'll tell them it's for the Hold. They won't believe me.
I'll trade this for something better and tell the other side it's a gift from a friend. Everyone's pleased. Especially me.
The road's been kind. Gave me you. And a gift. Two good things from one road.
Everything's useful in a ruin. Mostly because everything in it is broken.
Useful. Brute keeps.
Fine. Thanks. Say it once.
For me? It's not gold. But it's from you! I like yours.
Is it a treat? It's a treat! Or a weapon! Either way!

neutral: What is it? Huh. Fine. I'll find a use. Or I'll throw it at {neighbour}.
That's not gold. Did you know that's not gold? Just checking.
Hm. Thanks. It goes on the pile of things that aren't gold. Big pile, that one.
A gift is a gift. Not a good one. But a gift.

neutral.text: Hrm. Not gold.
Is it gold? It's not gold. Fine. I'll keep it anyway.
It isn't gold. It isn't food. It isn't even a good weapon. What is it for? Hm. I'll keep it so you can't take it back.
A gift for a Piglin that isn't gold. Bold. I admire boldness. I don't admire this. But the boldness, yes.
Is it a puzzle? A joke? A threat? Let me know when you decide.
I'll put it with the other mysteries. {neighbour} collects those. They'll lose it by the next feast.
Thank you, I think. I'll know when I find out what it does.
It's heavy. Is it gold? It's not gold. Then it's just heavy. I'll lift it for you. No. Not for you. I'll just lift it.
I accept. I accept with doubt. Next time bring something that shines.
A bit of nothing from a friend is still something. A small something. I'm counting it.
Odd gift. Odd person. Odd world. I can respect odd. I can't eat odd.
Do I keep it, trade it, or throw it at somebody? Let me think. Throw it at {neighbour}. Done.
From a friend I'll take anything. From an enemy, only gold. See how it works?
You thought of me. That counts for more than the thing. Don't tell the thing I said that.
Not metal, not gold, not even pretty. A shape I can work into something? No? Then it's a shape.
Could I shoot it? Could I skin it? Could I hide behind it? Fine. I'll sit on it.
I'd melt it, but I don't know what it is. That's never stopped me before. Stand back.
Would a hoglin eat it? Let me watch. If it does, it's food. If not, it's art.
I'll give you a nugget and a half for it. It's worth nothing. But it's your gift, so I'll pretend.
I've pulled stranger things from the ground. And stranger things from my teeth. Thank you.
I'll carry it a while. If it gets heavy I'll leave it under a stone for the next wanderer. A mystery for a mystery.
The Bastion's full of things like that. Things we don't understand. Welcome to the collection.
Not gold. Not food. Hrm. Keep anyway.
Strange. Brute will look at it. Later.
What is it? A toy? A weapon? A tooth?! Can I bite it?
Is it magic? It looks like it could be magic! Or a rock! Rocks are good!

disliked: Get that away from me! What are you, a Withren?
Rot! Ash! Bad luck! Take it back. Take it far back.
Is this a joke? Ha. Ha. Not funny. Take it away before I get funny.
You hand a Piglin THIS? Walk carefully, gold-wearer.

disliked.text: Hrm. No.
Ew! No! That's horrible! I'm telling!
Blue-fire stuff! Ghastly! Get it out of my sight before I decide you meant it.
Is this what the Withren give guests? Because I'm not a Withren. I'm warm.
Take it back. Take it away. Take it into the lava. No. Not into the lava. Never into the lava. Just away.
That smells like a grave and a grudge. Together! Congratulations.
Put that down. Put it down slowly. Now step back, and we'll agree you made a mistake.
Grey? Pale? Blue? Rotted? Whatever it is, I'll have none of it.
No. Just no. And then, in case that wasn't clear: no.
Bad luck wrapped in worse luck. Keep it, throw it, bury it. But not here.
I'm trying to be polite. It's not working. Take it away before politeness stops.
Friend or not, that's an insult. I'll forgive it once. That was the once.
You KNOW better. Somebody's tricked you, I can see it on your face. Who? Give me a name.
That smells of something dead. I've hunted worse. I just don't hold it.
Dull, grey, bad luck. Not in my forge. Not in my hand. Not on my anvil.
Even my hoglins would walk round that. And they eat boots.
Nothing in the ring has ever been worth less. I'd pay you nothing for it, and we'd both be better off.
I've left things like that on the ground a hundred times. For a reason. Put it back where you found it.
I knew a fellow who carried that around. He didn't see the next ghast coming.
The Bastion has enough bad luck. Please don't bring any more in. We're full.
Hrm. No. Take. Out.
Bad. Away. Now.
Ew! Ew ew ew! It's yucky! Get it away! I'm telling on you!
That's not shiny AT ALL! It's the opposite of shiny! Un-shiny!
My mother says never touch that! My mother says it's bad! My mother says lots of things!

again: You already gave me something. I'm greedy, not stupid. Well. Greedy. Come back later.
Another one? Ha! Keep it for next time. I'll be just as greedy then.
No more! I'm still admiring the last one.
Slow down. Give me everything now and what will you bribe me with later?

again.text: Hrm. Enough.
You already gave me a thing! Grown-ups say one is polite. I say more is better. But fine.
Another? Slow down. I only have so much room in my arms and in my heart. Mostly arms.
I'm still polishing the last one. Come back when it's dull.
You gave me something already. Take two in a row and I owe you a thing, and I hate owing.
One gift a visit, no more. That's good manners. I made it up just now. It's still the rule.
Easy, open-handed one! Save some for next time. Make me wait. I love waiting. I'm terrible at it.
Hold on, hold on. I'm still deciding whether I like you for the first one.
Not now! I'm in the middle of showing the last one off. Look at it. It's looking at you.
I can't carry any more. My hands are full of the last thing and my head's full of what I'm going to say about it.
Wait for the horn. Then give me whatever you like. I'll lose track of how many.
Don't spoil me. Spoil me later.
A friend who gives twice gets friends who give three times. Hold it for next time. I'll count it for you.
Let me finish admiring the first. A good gift needs time to settle.
My hands are full, one with the gift and one with the crossbow. Give me a moment.
One's enough. I've a furnace to watch. Take another and I'll forget the furnace, and then we'll both be sorry.
Another? You'll make the hoglins jealous. They can smell a gift. They'll come for it.
Another gift? Is that a bribe? A gift gets a smile. A bribe gets a discount. Which is it?
Another? Everything I own is on my back and the strap is already creaking. Next time, friend.
Give it to me next time. I'll leave room.
Another gift! A feast indeed. But keep it for the next visit. I'll lose it in the rubble otherwise.
Already took. Later.
Hrm. Hands full.
More?! But I'm still looking at the first one! Wait. Wait. Hold on. *snort* Fine. Hold it for me?
I only have two hands! One for the first, one for hitting {neighbour}!

empty: Your hand's empty. I can see it's empty. Why are you showing me an empty hand?
Nothing? You offer a Piglin nothing? Bold.
An empty hand is a sad thing. Fill it. With gold, ideally.
Ha! The old empty-hand trick. Very funny. Now give me something real.

empty.text: Hrm. Empty.
There's nothing in your hand! Is it invisible gold? Can I have the invisible gold?
You've nothing there. I checked. Twice. If you're teasing me, I'll tease back. With a fist.
An empty hand! Are you hiding it? Behind the other hand? Show me the other hand!
If your hand's empty, why hold it out? Is it a handshake? It's a poor handshake.
There's nothing in your hand but air. I don't take air. I'm not a ghast.
Ha. Empty. You came to a Piglin with nothing. Brave or hungry. Probably both.
First rule: don't wave an empty hand at a Piglin. Second rule: see the first rule.
The empty-handed gift is the oldest joke there is. I'll laugh once. There. Done.
I'll accept the thought. Thoughts don't shine. Next time bring a thought and a nugget.
You came with empty hands and I'm glad you came. Don't tell the others.
Friends can show up with empty hands. I never said that. Fill them next time. I'll know if you don't.
You hold your hand out like a bowl with nothing in it. Want me to put something there? I'd put a rock. Hold still.
My eyes are good, you know. Good at gold means good at spotting where there isn't any.
An empty hand has one good use: gripping a hammer. Pick something up. Anything. I'll fix it.
Not even a scrap of fungus? Empty! I've bagged bigger prizes off a pebble.
Nothing to melt means nothing for me. Go find something and come back smelling of smoke.
Even a hoglin comes with a bit of dirt on it. You come with nothing. Remarkable.
Nothing to trade. Shocking. Want to see my face when I'm shocked? Look! There. Done.
I've seen empty hands before. Usually on a road with no end. Come eat, then fill them.
Empty hands are all that's left in the Bastion. We call them visitors' hands. Fill them and we'll call them friends' hands.
Nothing. Hrm. Move along.
Empty hand. Brute watching. Hrm.
Nothing?! Check your other hand! The other other hand!
Is it invisible? Is it a ghost nugget? Ghost nuggets don't count!

levelup.text: You came back! Nobody comes back. Fine, you're a Shiny Stranger now. Here, five nuggets. Don't spend them. Admire them.
Hrm. You came back. Fine.
You came back! You're my Shiny Stranger! Here, a nugget. It's only a bit bitten.
Nugget-friend! I told {neighbour} all about you. Well, I said 'the shiny one'. Here, eat. Thin folk drop their gold.
Ingot-friend! Two ingots: one to keep, one to give back to me. That's friendship. And I know your face now. Gold or no gold, I won't swing at you.
Ingot-friend. Know your face now. No gold, fine. I won't swing. Vault's still mine.
Ingot-friend! Here, a whole ingot! And you don't have to be shiny for me now. I'll know it's you.
Hoard-friend. You may stand at the Hoard gate and nobody hits you first. Take my second-best sword. The best one is mine.
TUSK-KIN! Everyone hear it! Take this. Out of an old bastion vault, kept since the fire. Eat it or keep it. I'd keep it.
Tusk-kin. Take axe. Spare one. Good axe.
You're my Tusk-kin forever! Here, my best treasure. I found it. Mostly found it. Don't tell {neighbour}.
Hah! The shiny one remembers the way! Take these, Shiny Stranger. Three nuggets and my good wishes. The wishes are free.
Shiny Stranger! That's your name now. It's better than Pink-skin. Pink-skin is a warning. Shiny Stranger is a hello.
You've come back twice! Most come once, take a swing and leave. You're different. Probably. Here, a few bolts for luck.
Hrm. Know you now. Stand behind the line, not on it.
You came back! I told everyone you were real. They said the grown-ups made you up to scare us into eating!
Nugget-friend! Now you're somebody I'd lend an axe to. Not my best axe. A decent axe. Here, eat. It's still warm.
Nugget-friend means I'd share a nugget with you. Half of one. And watch you bite it. Here, half a handful.
You know my name, I know yours, and {neighbour} is jealous. That's friendship. Take these. I took them from the Bartermaster. No, I earned them. Mostly.
Nugget-friend. Brute doesn't joke. Brute means it.
You're my nugget-friend! That's only the start! After that comes ingot-friend, and I'm saving that. Here, half my snack.
Ingot-friend! Clack tusks with me. Harder. *clack* There. Now it's sealed. I'll know your face in any mob, gold or no gold. Take an ingot for the seal.
Ingot-friend now. Secret: I never liked anyone this fast. I'm worried about myself. Take a handful of nuggets before I change my mind.
Ingot-friend. I'll know you even without the shine. You've a look. Honest, but with edges. Here, quartz for your teeth. Chew it anyway.
Ingot-friend. Face known. Gate opens a crack. Not wide.
You're my Ingot-friend! I'll know you without the shine and shout your name from far away! Here's my best chewing quartz!
Hoard-friend! My whole clan will hear it. Not the grumpy ones. The loud ones. Take my second-best crossbow. Mind the bolt. It's real.
Hoard-friend. Only trusted hands touch the Hoard. I won't let you touch it. But you may look closely, for a long time. One ingot for each look. Here, three.
I told my longhouse. They said nobody is that good a friend. Then you walked in. Nobody argued. Take these boots: gold on the toes, hide on the heels.
Hoard-friend. Hrm. Hand. Take.
You're my Hoard-friend! I trust you with my second-best secret! The best one is under the hearth. Wait, I forgot it. Take this.
TUSK-KIN! The highest word we have. It means family with a different face. Take this gold block. Not the Hold's. Mine, kept since before my tusks came in.
Tusk-kin. In the old times, kin shared the Hoard. Now I share my share. Keep it from the Brutes. Here are five ingots, and I'll count them again later.
You're kin! My name's yours, my clan's yours, my debts are... let's not talk about debts. Take the finest thing I own that isn't gold: a shroomlight from my first raid.
Tusk-kin. Brute remembers. Brute never forgets. Take.
TUSK-KIN! The best one! You have to be my friend till I'm old and wrinkly and loud! I saved my whole share of the feast for you!

farewell: Keep your gold on out there. Somebody always wants it. Usually me.

farewell.text: Off you go, shiny. Don't take that gold off until you're far away. Very far.
Off you go. Put some gold on before you pass the others. They don't know you like I do.

farewell: Leaving already? Ha! Fine. I'll tell everyone you couldn't keep up.
Don't let your world rot you. Come back shining.

farewell.text: Hrm. Go.
Bye! Bring gold next time! Lots!
Bye! *snort* Race you to the edge! I win!
Mind the broken bridges on your way out. The lava is patient.
Tell everyone {village} was the loudest Hold you ever saw. Because it was.
Go well, Tusk-kin. Anyone gives you trouble, tell me their name. I'll shout it at them.
Next time bring more ingots. I'm worth more ingots.

farewell: Off with you! And don't spend your gold where I can't see it.
Fine. Leave. I'll go back to counting.
Walk loud, walk shiny, walk home.
Mind the lava. It never says goodbye. It just takes.

farewell.text: Go on. Take your shine somewhere else. I'll miss it. A bit. Not much.

farewell: We'll talk again. Or shout. Either's fine.
Remember that I was nice to you. If anyone asks.
Don't stray from the paths. Lava is hungry and it waits for the careless.
Go! Boast of me wherever you walk. Make me taller.
Leave, then. I'll count in peace. I'll miss counting with someone watching.
Your boots are already pointing away from me. Follow them.

farewell.text: I'd say stay, but I've got work. And you've got legs.

farewell: Remember: shout last. It's the only rule that matters.
Don't thank me. Give me a nugget instead. Next time.
Come back with a story worth shouting.

farewell.text: Keep that gold polished where the others see it. A dull shine makes a dull friend.
Wear it proud. Nobody ever got stabbed for being too shiny. Well. Some did. Not you.
The gold stays on all the way home. And a bit longer, to be sure.
Gold on, chin up, hands off other people's chests.
Go, shine. When you come back I'll have a story for each of your scratches.
Put it on before you step out, friend. Out there only the shine speaks for you.
Out you go, bare as a bone. Watch the corners. I can't follow you.
I'll vouch for you here. I can't vouch for you out there. Wear your gold past the gate.
Go on, then. If anyone swings, shout my name. They'll still swing, but they'll be confused.
I'll remember your face. Make sure it comes back to me still attached.
Bare is fine with me. Out there, the gold stays on. That's the rule for everyone who isn't me. Don't forget it, friend.
Go on. Don't think we're friends yet. Come back and we'll see.
Good. You didn't steal anything. That's a high bar and you cleared it.
Right, go. Keep your gold on. I'll keep my hand on my axe. Nothing personal.
See you, shiny. I'll have more to say next time. And louder.
Come back soon. Not too soon. A little soon.
Go on, and tell them I said hello. Loudly.
Go safe, Ingot-friend. If anyone asks, say you know me. It'll scare them. Or save you.
Come back soon. It's too quiet without you. Imagine me saying that.
Hoard-friend, take care. There's a spot at my fire for you. Don't make me say it twice.
Go well, friend. I'll save the best stories for when you return.
Take a nugget for the road. No? Fine. I'll keep it for next time.
Tusk-kin, you carry my name when you walk. Walk loud.
Wherever you go, you're kin. Don't let the Rotted forget it.
If you need me, shout. I'll hear you. I always hear what I'm listening for.
Come back richer! The ring is always open. For ingots. For nuggets it's open a little.
Leaving? Prices go up when you leave. Come back soon.
Tell your friends about the ring. Tell your enemies too. They'll pay more.
Gold is easier to lose than to win. I know. I've done both. Go carefully.
Haggle hard out there. The best deals go to the loudest throat.
Keep low and quiet. Hoglins smell loud boots from far off.
Good luck out there. If you find tracks, they're mine. Bring me the news.
If you spot a big one, don't shoot it. Yell for me. I need the story.
Go quiet. The crimson hears everything and tells the hoglins.
Don't hunt anything bigger than you. Unless you bring it back. Then it's fine.
Don't step on my wart on your way out. I'll know.
If you find shroomlight, remember who showed you the fungus. Me. Remember me.
Mind the Weft nets in the canopy. If you get caught, shout my name. It might make them laugh.
I'd give you a fungus for the road, but I'm keeping them all. Take a smell. It's free.
If the canopy drips on you, that's shroomlight sap. Collect it. Tell no one. Tell me.
Off you go, before you catch fire. Not my fault if you catch fire.
Take care of your eyebrows out there. Mine are a warning.
Come back when the molds are full. A full mold is a happy Piglin.
If anyone is rude to you, melt them. Slowly. With joy.
Go well. The furnace stays hot till you're back. It's a promise. And an accident.
Keep your helmet polished. Cracks start where the shine stops.
If a rivet slips, come straight back. Don't let a stranger fix it. They'll ruin it.
Look after that armour. My work is on half the shoulders in the Nether.
Wear it well. Wear it loud.
If a thief eyes your gold, tell them a Goldsmith made it and knows exactly where the seams are.
Careful, the road smells of warped fungus. Don't let the hoglins catch the scent on you.
Go on, and think of me when you hear a snort. That's me saying farewell. Or a hoglin.
Come visit the young ones again. They grow so fast. Faster than my patience.
Don't wave at hoglins out there. They take it as a challenge.
Gristle will miss you. Gristle misses everyone who feeds him.
Same road, different stop. See you down it, friend.
If you hear news, shout it across the wastes. I'll catch it.
I'm going the other way. That's what makes a road. Two ways, and each of us thinks we picked right.
Go on, I'll be on the same road in a while. Probably behind you. Probably cursing you.
Mind the roads. They bend wherever the Rotted walk.
Take the left stairs down. The right ones are only good for falling.
Go carefully. The ghasts have seen you already. They just haven't decided.
You can come back through the broken door any time. We'll keep it broken for you.
Out you go. Leave the warm rooms warm.
The Brute says the vault stays shut while you're gone. He means it. He means everything.
Gate opens. Go through. Hrm.
Go. Safe. Hrm.
Walk straight. Don't look back. Hrm.
Come back. Same place. Same me.
Stay shiny.
Careful out there. Make it back. Hrm.
No gold, no entry. Remember. Hrm.
Bye! Don't forget me! I'll be here! Always! Mostly!
Come back soon! I'll have a new scab to show you!
Bye, shiny! Take care of your gold! Or give it to me!
Don't go! No, go. No, don't. Go, but come back.
I'll tell everyone you're my friend! Even the Brutes!
Race you to the... oh. You're going. Bye!
Bye! I'll hide a nugget for you! Where? Secret!
Wave! Wave back! Good, now I know you're real.
See you! I'll be bigger. Taller. With tusks.
Bring a baby hoglin next time! A clean one! Not clean? Fine!
Bye! Don't forget your shiny next time! I'll lend you mine! It's a pebble!
Come back! Come back! I'll wait under the table!
Bye! Mind the holes! I know where they all are! I fell in most of them!
Bye! Run past the horn tower quick! The Brute sneezes there!
Leave the way you came in. Different ways have different holes.
Back out through the broken door, then. Tell nobody where the warm rooms are.
Lava below, ghasts above, us in the middle. Walk straight and don't look at either.
Come back to {village} any time. We'll be loud. We're always loud.
Tell them at the next Hold that {village} sent you. They'll flinch. That's respect.
If the horn blows after you leave, it wasn't me. Probably.
Safe road. Out here it's you, the lava and luck. Mostly luck.
Keep your back to a wall and your gold to the front.
Nobody out here but us and the lava. Walk like someone's watching. Someone is.
Off with you! The Brutes are watching and I'd rather they saw us part as friends.
Put that ingot away before you go. I'm weak. Be kind.
Spend the nugget wisely. Better yet, don't spend it.
I'd walk you out, but my knee has opinions. Go on. I'll shout after you.
Go on. I'll tell the others you left bravely. I won't mention the shaking.
Sleep on gold, dream of gold, wake up richer. That's the whole blessing.

refuse.text: You hit me! Gold or no gold, I'm hitting back!
THIEF! Hoard-thief! Somebody blow the horn!
No talk! Only swinging now!
Your shiny helmet won't save you now!
Friend or not, you don't do that! Stand still so I can hit you!
Thief in the Bastion! To the vault, everyone! Don't let them out!
HRRAAH!
You're mean! I'm getting a Brute! A big one!
Hit me, will you? I'll hit you until the lava cools.
Wrong Piglin to swing at! Wrong! Wrong! WRONG!
I'm done talking. My fists have taken over.
You brought gold AND a fight. I'll keep the gold.
Shiny helmet, dull manners! Let me fix that.
Words are finished. Now we use tusks.
Swing at me again. Go on. I'm ready this time.
